property/AnimationTrack/Length.title: Length

property/AnimationTrack/Looped.description:
Sets whether the animation will repeat after finishing. If it is changed
while playing the result will take effect after the animation finishes.

This property sets whether the animation will repeat after finishing. If
it is changed while playing the result will take effect after the
animation finishes.

This property defaults to how it was set in the
[Animation Editor](../../../animation/editor.md). However, this property
can be changed, allowing control over the `Class.AnimationTrack` while it
is running. This property also correctly handles animations played in
reverse (negative `Class.AnimationTrack.Speed`). After the first keyframe
is reached, it will restart at the last keyframe.
property/AnimationTrack/Looped.title: Looped

property/AnimationTrack/Priority.description:
Sets the priority of an `Class.AnimationTrack`. Depending on what this is
set to, playing multiple animations at once will look to this property to
figure out which `Class.Keyframe` `Class.Pose|Poses` should be played over
one another.

This property sets the priority of an `Class.AnimationTrack`. Depending on
what this is set to, playing multiple animations at once will look to this
property to figure out which `Class.Keyframe` poses should be played over
one another. It uses `Enum.AnimationPriority` which has 7 priority levels:

1. `Enum.AnimationPriority|Action4` (highest priority)
2. `Enum.AnimationPriority|Action3`
3. `Enum.AnimationPriority|Action2`
4. `Enum.AnimationPriority|Action`
5. `Enum.AnimationPriority|Movement`
6. `Enum.AnimationPriority|Idle`
7. `Enum.AnimationPriority|Core` (lowest priority)

Properly set animation priorities, either through the
[Animation Editor](../../../animation/editor.md) or through this property,
allow multiple animations to be played without them clashing. Where two
playing animations direct the target to move the same limb in different
ways, the `Class.AnimationTrack` with the highest priority will show. If
both animations have the same priority, the weights of the tracks will be
used to combine the animations.
property/AnimationTrack/Priority.title: Priority

property/AnimationTrack/Speed.description:
Read-only property that gives the current playback speed of the
`Class.AnimationTrack`.

This read-only property gives the current playback speed of the
`Class.AnimationTrack`. When equal to `1`, the amount of time an animation
takes to complete is equal to `Class.AnimationTrack.Length`, in seconds.

If the speed is adjusted through `Class.AnimationTrack:AdjustSpeed()`, the
actual time it will take a track to play can be computed by dividing the
length by the speed. Speed is a unitless quantity.
property/AnimationTrack/Speed.title: Speed

property/AnimationTrack/TimePosition.description:
Returns the position in time in seconds that an `Class.AnimationTrack` is
through playing its source animation. Can be set to make the track jump to
a specific moment in the animation.

Returns the position in time in seconds that an `Class.AnimationTrack` is
through playing its source animation. Can be set to make the track jump to
a specific moment in the animation, but the `Class.AnimationTrack` must be
playing to do so. It can also be used in combination with
`Class.AnimationTrack:AdjustSpeed()` to freeze the animation at a desired
point by setting speed to `0`.
property/AnimationTrack/TimePosition.title: TimePosition

property/AnimationTrack/WeightCurrent.description:
Read-only property that gives the current weight of the
`Class.AnimationTrack`.

When weight is set in an `Class.AnimationTrack` it does not change
instantaneously but moves from `Class.AnimationTrack.WeightCurrent` to
`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightTarget`. The time it takes to do this is
determined by the `fadeTime` parameter given when the animation is played,
or the weight is adjusted.

`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightCurrent` can be checked against
`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightTarget` to see if the desired weight has been
reached. Note that these values should not be checked for equality with
the `==` operator, as both of these values are floats. To see if
`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightCurrent` has reached the target weight, it is
recommended to see if the distance between those values is sufficiently
small.
property/AnimationTrack/WeightCurrent.title: WeightCurrent

property/AnimationTrack/WeightTarget.description:
Read-only property that gives the current weight of the
`Class.AnimationTrack`.

This read-only property gives the current weight of the
`Class.AnimationTrack`. It has a default value of `1` and is set when
`Class.AnimationTrack:Play()`, `Class.AnimationTrack:Stop()` or
`Class.AnimationTrack:AdjustWeight()` is called. When weight is set in an
`Class.AnimationTrack` it does not change instantaneously but moves from
`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightCurrent` to
`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightTarget`. The time it takes to do this is
determined by the `fadeTime` parameter given when the animation is played,
or the weight is adjusted.

`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightCurrent` can be checked against
`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightTarget` to see if the desired weight has been
reached. Note that these values should not be checked for equality with
the `==` operator, as both of these values are floats. To see if
`Class.AnimationTrack.WeightCurrent` has reached the target weight, it is
recommended to see if the distance between those values is sufficiently
small.
property/AnimationTrack/WeightTarget.title: WeightTarget

property/Animator/EvaluationThrottled.description:
Indicates whether animation evaluation was throttled (skipped) this frame
for this `Class.Animator`.

A read-only property that indicates whether animation evaluation was
throttled (skipped) on this frame. When `true`, the `Class.Animator`
reused the pose from the previous frame instead of evaluating fresh
animation data.

This property is useful when layering procedural animation on top of
`Class.AnimationConstraint.Transform|Transform` — if evaluation was
throttled, applying procedural offsets would fight the stale pose and
should be skipped:
property/Animator/EvaluationThrottled.title: EvaluationThrottled

property/Animator/PreferLodEnabled.description:
Controls whether animation LOD throttling is allowed for this
`Class.Animator`. When set to `false`, animations always evaluate at full
fidelity.

When `true` (the default), the engine may reduce animation evaluation
frequency for remotely-simulated characters based on distance, screen
coverage, and frame budget. When set to `false`, LOD-based throttling is
disabled and this `Class.Animator` always evaluates at full fidelity.

Setting this to `false` is useful for important NPCs or characters that
must always animate smoothly regardless of distance. However, disabling
LOD for many animators simultaneously can impact performance.

Note that this property only controls per-animator LOD throttling. The
workspace-level `Class.Workspace.ClientAnimatorThrottlingMode` setting can
independently disable or enable throttling for all animators.
property/Animator/PreferLodEnabled.title: PreferLodEnabled

property/ArcHandles/Axes.description: Sets the current Axes ArcHandles will show.
property/ArcHandles/Axes.title: Axes

property/AssetDeliveryProxy/Interface.description:
The network interface address that the asset-delivery HTTP server binds
to.

Sets the local network interface (address) that the proxy's HTTP server
binds to when it starts. Defaults to an empty string. Assigning a value
schedules the server to restart, but a new interface only takes effect
while the server is running — that is, once
`Class.AssetDeliveryProxy.StartServer` is `true` (it defaults to `false`).
property/AssetDeliveryProxy/Interface.title: Interface

property/AssetDeliveryProxy/Port.description:
The TCP port that the asset-delivery HTTP server listens on.

The TCP port the proxy's HTTP server listens on. Defaults to `0`, which
tells the server to pick an available port automatically. While the server
is running, reading this property returns the port actually in use rather
than the configured value. A new port only takes effect when the server
(re)starts via `Class.AssetDeliveryProxy.StartServer` (defaults to
`false`).
property/AssetDeliveryProxy/Port.title: Port

property/AssetDeliveryProxy/StartServer.description:
Controls whether the asset-delivery HTTP server is running.

Controls whether the proxy's HTTP server is running. Setting it to `true`
schedules the server to start; setting it to `false` stops it. Defaults to
`false`, so the server is off until you enable it. Because the server only
(re)starts while this is `true`, changes to
`Class.AssetDeliveryProxy.Interface` and `Class.AssetDeliveryProxy.Port`
take effect only when this property is `true`.
property/AssetDeliveryProxy/StartServer.title: StartServer

property/AssetPatchSettings/ContentId.description:
The content ID used to override this patch asset when it is served by
`Class.AssetDeliveryProxy`.

The content ID used to override this asset when it is served by
`Class.AssetDeliveryProxy`, for example
`rbxasset://models/DataModelPatch/DataModelPatch.rbxm`. When
`Class.IncrementalPatchBuilder` finishes a build, it registers the
serialized patch under this content ID so that requests for that asset
return the patched content. Defaults to an empty string.
property/AssetPatchSettings/ContentId.title: ContentId

property/AssetPatchSettings/OutputPath.description:
The filesystem path where the built patch asset is cached; when empty, an
in-memory cache is used instead.

The output path for the local cache of the patch asset, for example
`/path/to/content/models/DataModelPatch/DataModelPatch.rbxm`. When set,
`Class.IncrementalPatchBuilder` writes each completed patch to this path,
creating any missing parent directories. Defaults to an empty string; when
empty, no file is written and an in-memory cache is used instead.
property/AssetPatchSettings/OutputPath.title: OutputPath

property/AssetPatchSettings/PatchId.description:
An identifier for distinguishing patches under a single
`Class.IncrementalPatchBuilder`. Has no effect.

An identifier for distinguishing patches under a single
`Class.IncrementalPatchBuilder`. Has no effect. Defaults to an empty
string.
property/AssetPatchSettings/PatchId.title: PatchId

property/AssetService/AllowInsertFreeAss.description:
Controls whether `Class.AssetService:LoadAssetAsync()` can load assets
that are not owned by the experience creator.

This property can only be modified in Studio's **Experience Settings** by
changing **Allow Loading Third Party Assets**.

When `false` (default), `Class.AssetService:LoadAssetAsync()` can only
load assets that meet one of the following:

- The asset must be **created or owned** by the game creator.
- The asset must be **shared** by the asset owner.
- The asset must be owned by Roblox.

When `true`, `Class.AssetService:LoadAssetAsync()` can additionally load
any public free asset on the Creator Store.
property/AssetService/AllowInsertFreeAss.title: AllowInsertFreeAssets

property/Atmosphere/Color.description:
Changes the `Class.Atmosphere` hue for subtle environmental moods.

A `Datatype.Color3` value which changes the `Class.Atmosphere` hue for
subtle environmental moods. This is best combined with increased
`Class.Atmosphere.Haze` to expand the visible effect.
property/Atmosphere/Color.title: Color

property/Atmosphere/Decay.description:
When used with increased `Class.Atmosphere.Haze` and
`Class.Atmosphere.Glare`, defines the hue of the `Class.Atmosphere` away
from the sun, gradually falling off from `Class.Atmosphere.Color` towards
this value.

Defines the hue of the `Class.Atmosphere` away from the sun, gradually
falling off from `Class.Atmosphere.Color` towards this value. Must be used
with `Class.Atmosphere.Haze` and `Class.Atmosphere.Glare` levels higher
than 0 to see any effect.
property/Atmosphere/Decay.title: Decay

property/Atmosphere/Density.description:
Defines the amount of particles in the `Class.Atmosphere` and essentially
controls how much in-game objects/terrain will be obscured by them.

Defines the amount of particles in the air. The higher the density, the
more particles and the more in-game objects/terrain will be obscured by
them. Note that density does not **directly** affect the skybox — it
merely affects in-game objects/terrain and visibility of the skybox
through them.
property/Atmosphere/Density.title: Density

property/Atmosphere/Glare.description:
When used with increased `Class.Atmosphere.Haze`, specifies the glow/glare
of the `Class.Atmosphere` around the sun. More glare results in an
increased effect of sunlight cast onto the sky and world.

Specifies the glow/glare of the `Class.Atmosphere` around the sun. More
glare results in an increased effect of sunlight cast onto the sky and
world. Must be used with a `Class.Atmosphere.Haze` level higher than 0 to
see any effect.
property/Atmosphere/Glare.title: Glare

property/Atmosphere/Haze.description:
Defines the haziness of the `Class.Atmosphere` with a visible effect both
above the horizon and into the distance.

Defines the haziness of the `Class.Atmosphere` with a visible effect both
above the horizon and into the distance. This can be combined with
`Class.Atmosphere.Color` to create environmental moods, like a grey tint
for a polluted alien planet.
property/Atmosphere/Haze.title: Haze

property/Atmosphere/Offset.description:
Controls how light transmits between the camera and the sky background.

Controls how light transmits between the camera and the sky background.
Increase this value to create a horizon silhouette against the sky or
reduce it to blend distant objects into the sky for an endless and
seamless open world.

Offset should be balanced against `Class.Atmosphere.Density` and carefully
tested in your place. A low offset may cause "ghosting" where the skybox
can be seen through objects/terrain. This can be corrected by increasing
the offset, which more clearly silhouettes distant objects/terrain against
the sky, but too much offset may reveal level-of-detail "popping" for far
distant terrain and meshes.
property/Atmosphere/Offset.title: Offset

property/AtmosphereSensor/AirDensity.description: Measures the density of the air where the sensor is positioned.
property/AtmosphereSensor/AirDensity.title: AirDensity

property/AtmosphereSensor/RelativeWindVe.description: Reports the wind velocity relative to the sensor.
property/AtmosphereSensor/RelativeWindVe.title: RelativeWindVelocity

property/Attachment/Axis.description:
Direction of the **X** axis of the attachment, represented as a unit
`Datatype.Vector3`.

Direction of the **X** axis of the attachment, represented as a unit
`Datatype.Vector3`. Together with
`Class.Attachment.SecondaryAxis|SecondaryAxis`, this property defines the
orientation of the attachment. Setting `Axis` automatically re-projects
`SecondaryAxis` onto the plane perpendicular to the new axis so the two
always remain orthogonal.

The default value is `(1, 0, 0)`.
property/Attachment/Axis.title: Axis

property/Attachment/CFrame.description:
`Datatype.CFrame` offset of the attachment.

The `Datatype.CFrame` offset of the attachment. Changes to this property
will reflect onto the `Class.Attachment.Position|Position` and
`Class.Attachment.Rotation|Rotation` properties of this object. Similarly,
a change to either of those properties will reflect onto this property.
property/Attachment/CFrame.title: CFrame

property/Attachment/Orientation.description:
Orientation of the attachment relative to the orientation of its parent.

Orientation of the attachment relative to the orientation of its parent.
Rotations are in **Z**, **X**, **Y** order.
property/Attachment/Orientation.title: Orientation

property/Attachment/Position.description:
Positional offset of the attachment, relative to the position and
orientation of its parent.

Positional offset of the attachment, relative to the position and
orientation of its parent. This value corresponds to the translational
component of `Class.Attachment.CFrame|CFrame`; changing either property
updates the other. The offset is expressed in the local coordinate space
of the parent `Class.BasePart`, `Class.Bone`, or `Class.Attachment`.

The default value is `(0, 0, 0)`.
property/Attachment/Position.title: Position

property/Attachment/Rotation.deprecationMessage:
This property is deprecated and should not be used in new work. See
`Class.Attachment.Orientation|Orientation` instead.
property/Attachment/Rotation.description:
Rotation of the attachment relative to the rotation of its parent.

Rotation of the attachment relative to the rotation of its parent.
Rotations are in **Z**, **Y**, **X** order.
property/Attachment/Rotation.title: Rotation
property/Attachment/Rotation.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This property is deprecated and should not be used in new work. See
`Class.Attachment.Orientation|Orientation` instead.

property/Attachment/SecondaryAxis.description:
Direction of the **Y** axis of the attachment, represented as a unit
`Datatype.Vector3`.

Direction of the **Y** axis of the attachment, represented as a unit
`Datatype.Vector3`. Together with `Class.Attachment.Axis|Axis`, this
property defines the orientation of the attachment. When set, the value is
projected onto the plane perpendicular to `Axis` so the two axes always
remain orthogonal; the resulting stored value may therefore differ from
the value you assign.

The default value is `(0, 1, 0)`.
property/Attachment/SecondaryAxis.title: SecondaryAxis

property/Attachment/Visible.description:
Toggles the in-experience visibility of the attachment.

Toggles the in-experience visibility of the attachment. When set to
`true`, the attachment renders as a small green sphere at its world
position during gameplay. This is useful for debugging constraint setups
or verifying attachment placement without needing Studio's constraint
detail overlays.

The default value is `false`.
property/Attachment/Visible.title: Visible

property/Attachment/WorldAxis.description:
Direction of the **X** axis of the attachment relative to the world,
represented as a unit `Datatype.Vector3` with a length of 1.

Direction of the **X** axis of the attachment relative to the world,
represented as a unit `Datatype.Vector3` with a length of 1. This is the
world-space equivalent of `Class.Attachment.Axis|Axis`, computed by
transforming the local axis through the parent's `Datatype.CFrame`.
Setting this property converts the supplied direction into the parent's
local space and updates `Axis` accordingly.
property/Attachment/WorldAxis.title: WorldAxis

property/Attachment/WorldCFrame.description:
The exact `Datatype.CFrame` of the attachment in world space coordinates.

The exact `Datatype.CFrame` of the attachment in world space coordinates,
independent of its parent. The value of this property is equivalent to
multiplying the `Datatype.CFrame` of the attachment's parent by its own
`Datatype.CFrame`.
property/Attachment/WorldCFrame.title: WorldCFrame

property/Attachment/WorldOrientation.description:
Orientation of the attachment relative to the world rather than its own
parent.

Orientation of the attachment relative to the world rather than its own
parent. Rotations are in **Z**, **X**, **Y** order.
property/Attachment/WorldOrientation.title: WorldOrientation

property/Attachment/WorldPosition.description:
Position of the attachment relative to the world rather than its own
parent.

Position of the attachment relative to the world rather than its own
parent. This is the world-space equivalent of
`Class.Attachment.Position|Position`, computed by transforming the local
offset through the parent's `Datatype.CFrame`. Setting this property
converts the supplied position into the parent's local space and updates
`Position` accordingly.
property/Attachment/WorldPosition.title: WorldPosition

property/Attachment/WorldRotation.deprecationMessage:
This item has been superseded by
`Class.Attachment.WorldOrientation|WorldOrientation` which should be used
in new work.
property/Attachment/WorldRotation.description:
Rotation of the attachment relative to the world rather than its own
parent.
property/Attachment/WorldRotation.title: WorldRotation
property/Attachment/WorldRotation.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This item has been superseded by
`Class.Attachment.WorldOrientation|WorldOrientation` which should be used
in new work.

property/Attachment/WorldSecondaryAxis.description:
Direction of the **Y** axis of the attachment relative to the world,
represented as a unit `Datatype.Vector3` with a length of 1.

Direction of the **Y** axis of the attachment relative to the world,
represented as a unit `Datatype.Vector3` with a length of 1. This is the
world-space equivalent of `Class.Attachment.SecondaryAxis|SecondaryAxis`,
computed by transforming the local secondary axis through the parent's
`Datatype.CFrame`. Setting this property converts the supplied direction
into the parent's local space and updates `SecondaryAxis` accordingly.
property/Attachment/WorldSecondaryAxis.title: WorldSecondaryAxis

property/AudioAnalyzer/PeakLevel.description:
The loudest volume observed during the last audio buffer.

The loudest volume observed during the last audio buffer. This property
changes more often than the framerate and does not fire changed events. On
the server, this property is always `0`.
property/AudioAnalyzer/PeakLevel.title: PeakLevel

property/AudioAnalyzer/RmsLevel.description:
The root-mean-square average volume observed during the last audio buffer.

The root-mean-square average volume observed during the last audio buffer.
This property is generally more stable than
`Class.AudioAnalyzer.PeakLevel|PeakLevel` but it may not capture momentary
volume spikes. This property changes more often than the framerate and
does not fire changed events. On the server, this property is always `0`.
property/AudioAnalyzer/RmsLevel.title: RmsLevel

property/AudioAnalyzer/SpectrumEnabled.description:
Enables usage of `Class.AudioAnalyzer:GetSpectrum|GetSpectrum`.

Enables usage of `Class.AudioAnalyzer:GetSpectrum|GetSpectrum()`. If
`false`, `Class.AudioAnalyzer:GetSpectrum|GetSpectrum()` returns an empty
array, but the CPU overhead of the `Class.AudioAnalyzer` is dramatically
reduced. This means that if you are only analyzing the **volume** of an
audio stream, you can disable this property to improve performance.
property/AudioAnalyzer/SpectrumEnabled.title: SpectrumEnabled

property/AudioAnalyzer/WindowSize.description:
Controls the resolution and timeliness of
`Class.AudioAnalyzer:GetSpectrum|GetSpectrum`.

Controls the size of arrays returned by
`Class.AudioAnalyzer:GetSpectrum|GetSpectrum()`. Larger windows contain
more data (so more-accurate frequency responses) but change less often.
property/AudioAnalyzer/WindowSize.title: WindowSize

property/AudioChannelMixer/Layout.description:
Controls the output channel layout to be mixed to.

Controls the output channel layout to be mixed to. The **Input** pin of
`Class.AudioChannelMixer` is always forwarded "as-is" to **Output**, but
depending on the value of `Layout`:

- For `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Mono|Mono`, the **Center** pin consumes
  audio streams.
- For `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Stereo|Stereo`, the **Left** and **Right**
  pins consume audio streams.
- For `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Quad|Quad`, the **Left**, **Right**,
  **BackLeft**, and **BackRight** pins consume audio streams.
- `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Surround_5|Surround_5` is the same as `Quad`,
  plus **Center** consumes an audio stream.
- `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Surround_5_1|Surround_5_1` is the same as
  `Surround_5`, plus **Sub** consumes an audio stream.
- `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Surround_7_1|Surround_7_1` is the same as
  `Surround_5_1`, plus **SurroundLeft** and **SurroundRight** consume
  audio streams.
- For `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Surround_7_1_4|Surround_7_1_4`, all
  secondary input pins consume audio streams.
property/AudioChannelMixer/Layout.title: Layout

property/AudioChannelSplitter/Layout.description:
Controls the input channel layout to be split from.

Controls the input channel layout to be split from. When changed, all
audio streams prior to this channel splitter's input may need to be
up-mixed (widened to at least as many channels as the input requires).

The **Output** pin produces a copy of the stream wired to **Input** but,
depending on the value of `Class.AudioChannelSplitter.Layout`:

- For `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Mono|Mono`, the **Center** pin produces an
  audio stream.
- For `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Stereo|Stereo`, the **Left** and **Right**
  pins produce audio streams.
- For `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Quad|Quad`, the **Left**, **Right**,
  **BackLeft**, and **BackRight** pins produce audio streams.
- `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Surround_5|Surround_5` is the same as `Quad`,
  plus **Center** produces an audio stream.
- `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Surround_5_1|Surround_5_1` is the same as
  `Surround_5`, plus **Sub** produces an audio stream.
- `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Surround_7_1|Surround_7_1` is the same as
  `Surround_5_1`, plus **SurroundLeft** and **SurroundRight** produce
  audio streams.
- For `Enum.AudioChannelLayout.Surround_7_1_4|Surround_7_1_4`, all
  secondary output pins produce audio streams.
property/AudioChannelSplitter/Layout.title: Layout

property/AudioChorus/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioChorus/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioChorus/Depth.description:
Controls the maximum delay time of the copied streams in the chorus
effect.

Controls how strong the chorus effect is by changing the maximum delay
time of the copy streams. Ranges from 0 to 1 which corresponds to 0 to 100
milliseconds of maximum delay.
property/AudioChorus/Depth.title: Depth

property/AudioChorus/Mix.description:
Controls the balance of plain input stream to modified output stream.

Controls the balance of plain input stream to modified output stream.
Ranges from 0 to 1.
property/AudioChorus/Mix.title: Mix

property/AudioChorus/Rate.description:
Controls the rate of pitch modulations.

Frequency controlling the rate of pitch modulations, in hertz. Ranges from
0 to 20.
property/AudioChorus/Rate.title: Rate

property/AudioCompressor/Attack.description:
Controls how quickly the compressor will clamp down on volume after it
surpasses `Class.AudioCompressor.Threshold|Threshold`.

Time, in seconds, denoting how quickly the compressor will clamp down on
volume after it surpasses `Class.AudioCompressor.Threshold|Threshold`.
Ranges from 0.0001 to 0.5.
property/AudioCompressor/Attack.title: Attack

property/AudioCompressor/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioCompressor/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioCompressor/MakeupGain.description:
A gain value to be applied after compression.

Gain value to be applied after compression, in decibels. After limiting
the dynamic range, the resulting stream may be very quiet and this
property can be used to compensate. Ranges from -30 to 30.
property/AudioCompressor/MakeupGain.title: MakeupGain

property/AudioCompressor/Ratio.description:
Ratio of input volume to output volume, to be applied when surpassing
`Class.AudioCompressor.Threshold|Threshold`.

Ratio of input volume to output volume, to be applied when surpassing
`Class.AudioCompressor.Threshold|Threshold`. For example, a value of 2
will cut the amount by which the input stream exceeds the threshold in
half whenever the input stream does so. Ranges from 1 to 50.
property/AudioCompressor/Ratio.title: Ratio

property/AudioCompressor/Release.description:
Controls how quickly the compressor will unclamp after the stream volume
dips back below `Class.AudioCompressor.Threshold|Threshold`.

Time, in seconds, denoting how quickly the compressor will unclamp after
its stream volume dips back below
`Class.AudioCompressor.Threshold|Threshold`. Ranges from 0.01 to 5.
property/AudioCompressor/Release.title: Release

property/AudioCompressor/Threshold.description:
Gain value at which the compressor will start to modify the input stream.

Gain value at which the compressor will start to modify the input stream,
in decibels, with a range of -60 to 0. When the input stream's volume
surpasses `Class.AudioCompressor.Threshold|Threshold`, the compressor will
take `Class.AudioCompressor.Attack|Attack` seconds to kick in. When the
input stream's volume recedes below
`Class.AudioCompressor.Threshold|Threshold`, the compressor will take
`Class.AudioCompressor.Release|Release` seconds to stop acting.

If any `Class.Wire|Wires` are connected to the **Sidechain** pin of the
compressor, this threshold analyzes those streams instead of the **Input**
streams; this can be used to duck the volume of one stream in response to
another.
property/AudioCompressor/Threshold.title: Threshold

property/AudioDeviceInput/AccessType.description:
Determines whether the list of user IDs provided to
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.SetUserIdAccessList|SetUserIdAccessList` is
treated as an allow-list or deny-list.

Determines whether the list of user IDs provided to
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.SetUserIdAccessList|SetUserIdAccessList` is
treated as an allow-list or deny-list.

If `Class.AudioDeviceInput.AccessType|AccessType` is
`Enum.AccessModifierType.Allow`, then **only** the supplied user IDs are
**permitted** to hear this `Class.AudioDeviceInput`. If
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.AccessType|AccessType` is
`Enum.AccessModifierType.Deny`, then **only** the supplied user IDs are
**blocked** from hearing this `Class.AudioDeviceInput`.

Since player voices are networked, this property should only be assigned
from the server in order to replicate properly.
property/AudioDeviceInput/AccessType.title: AccessType

property/AudioDeviceInput/Active.description:
Controls whether the physical device is actively recording.

Controls whether the physical device is actively recording. This property
is only set by Roblox core scripts, but it may be read by user scripts.
Generally, an `Class.AudioDeviceInput` may only be producing sound if
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.Active|Active` is true **and**
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.Muted|Muted` is false.
property/AudioDeviceInput/Active.title: Active

property/AudioDeviceInput/IsReady.description:
Denotes whether this `Class.AudioDeviceInput` is ready to produce sound.

Denotes whether this `Class.AudioDeviceInput` is ready to produce sound,
meaning all network connections have been established.
property/AudioDeviceInput/IsReady.title: IsReady

property/AudioDeviceInput/Muted.description:
Controls whether this `Class.AudioDeviceInput` is muted.

Controls whether this `Class.AudioDeviceInput` is muted. Unlike
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.Active|Active`, this property is publicly
scriptable.

Generally, an `Class.AudioDeviceInput` may only be heard if
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.Active|Active` is true **and**
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.Muted|Muted` is false.
property/AudioDeviceInput/Muted.title: Muted

property/AudioDeviceInput/Player.description:
Determines whose device is producing sound.

Determines whose device is producing sound. In order to replicate
properly, this should only be assigned from the server. Assigning this
property locally generally does not work, unless
`Class.AudioDeviceInput.Player|Player` is `Class.Players.LocalPlayer`.
property/AudioDeviceInput/Player.title: Player

property/AudioDeviceInput/Volume.description:
Volume level which is multiplied onto the output audio stream.

Volume level which is multiplied onto the output audio stream. Ranges from
0 to 3.
property/AudioDeviceInput/Volume.title: Volume

property/AudioDeviceOutput/Player.description:
A `Class.Player` who is intended to hear the connected audio streams.

An optional `Class.Player` who is intended to hear the connected audio
streams. If left unspecified, the streams wired to this
`Class.AudioDeviceOutput` are heard by everyone.
property/AudioDeviceOutput/Player.title: Player

property/AudioDistortion/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioDistortion/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioDistortion/Level.description:
Controls how distorted the input stream will become.

Controls how distorted the input stream will become. Ranges from 0 to 1.
property/AudioDistortion/Level.title: Level

property/AudioEcho/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioEcho/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioEcho/DelayTime.description:
The amount of time between echoes.

The amount of time between echoes, in seconds. Ranges from 0.001 to 5.
property/AudioEcho/DelayTime.title: DelayTime

property/AudioEcho/DryLevel.description:
Gain level determining how loud the original, unaltered audio stream will
be.

Gain level, in decibels, determining how loud the original, unaltered
audio stream will be. Ranges from -80 to 10.
property/AudioEcho/DryLevel.title: DryLevel

property/AudioEcho/Feedback.description:
How slowly echoes fade away.

Determines how slowly echoes fade away, with a range of 0 to 1. A value of
0 means that only a single echo is heard, whereas a value of 1 means that
old echoes never fully disappear.
property/AudioEcho/Feedback.title: Feedback

property/AudioEcho/RampTime.description:
The time taken to interpolate between
`Class.AudioEcho.DelayTime|DelayTime` values.

The time, in seconds, the `Class.AudioEcho` takes to interpolate between
different `Class.AudioEcho.DelayTime|DelayTime` values, when changed. This
can be used to smooth out changes in the
`Class.AudioEcho.DelayTime|DelayTime`, or create a pitch bend effect when
the `Class.AudioEcho.DelayTime|DelayTime` is modified at a constant rate.
Ranges from 0 to 60000.
property/AudioEcho/RampTime.title: RampTime

property/AudioEcho/WetLevel.description:
Gain level determining how loud the echoed stream will be.

Gain level, in decibels, determining how loud the echoed stream will be.
Ranges from -80 to 10.
property/AudioEcho/WetLevel.title: WetLevel

property/AudioEmitter/AcousticSimulation.description:
Determines whether acoustic simulation should be used for this
`Class.AudioEmitter`.

Determines whether sound from this `Class.AudioEmitter` shoud
automatically implement features of acoustic simulation, such as occlusion
(being muffled through walls), diffraction (bending around corners), and
reverberation (echoing off of walls), when being heard by an
`Class.AudioListener|AudioListener`. Note that the `Class.AudioListener`
also needs its
`Class.AudioListener.AcousticSimulationEnabled|AcousticSimulationEnabled`
property set to `true` for the effects to occur.
property/AudioEmitter/AcousticSimulation.title: AcousticSimulationEnabled

property/AudioEmitter/AngleAttenuation.description:
Represents how the perceived volume of the emitted sound changes based on
the angle between a `Class.AudioListener` and the
`Datatype.CFrame.LookVector|LookVector` associated with the
`Class.AudioEmitter`.

Represents a volume-over-angle curve that affects how loudly a
`Class.AudioListener` will hear the `Class.AudioEmitter`, based on the
angle between them and the `Datatype.CFrame.LookVector|LookVector`
associated with the `Class.AudioEmitter`.

This property is internal and can't be accessed by scripts; it exists to
support replication. See
`Class.AudioEmitter:SetAngleAttenuation()|SetAngleAttenuation()` for usage
details.
property/AudioEmitter/AngleAttenuation.title: AngleAttenuation

property/AudioEmitter/AudioInteractionGr.description:
Controls which `Class.AudioListener|AudioListeners` are capable of hearing
this `Class.AudioEmitter`.

If an `Class.AudioEmitter` and an `Class.AudioListener` share an
interaction group, then the listener is capable of hearing the emitter.
property/AudioEmitter/AudioInteractionGr.title: AudioInteractionGroup

property/AudioEmitter/DiffractionEnabled.description:
Controls whether sound from this `Class.AudioEmitter` bends around corners
when acoustic simulation is active.

Controls whether diffraction (sound bending around corners) is applied to
this `Class.AudioEmitter` when heard by an `Class.AudioListener`. When set
to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`, the effective value is inherited from
`Class.SoundService`. When set to `Enum.SimulationMode.Enabled` or
`Enum.SimulationMode.Disabled`, it overrides the service-level setting for
this emitter.

Diffraction repositions the perceived audio source to the edge of an
obstacle. Both the `Class.AudioEmitter` and `Class.AudioListener` must
have diffraction effectively enabled for the effect to occur on their
audio path. Diffraction also requires occlusion to be enabled. If
occlusion is off, sound passes straight through obstacles, so it has no
reason to bend around corners and this property has no effect. Defaults to
`Enum.SimulationMode.Default`.
property/AudioEmitter/DiffractionEnabled.title: DiffractionEnabled

property/AudioEmitter/DistanceAttenuatio.description:
Represents how the perceived volume of the emitted sound changes as the
distance between a `Class.AudioListener` and the `Class.AudioEmitter`
increases.

Represents a volume-over-distance curve that affects how loudly a
`Class.AudioListener` will hear the `Class.AudioEmitter`, based on the
distance between them.

This property is internal and can't be accessed by scripts; it exists to
support replication. See
`Class.AudioEmitter:SetDistanceAttenuation()|SetDistanceAttenuation()` for
usage details.
property/AudioEmitter/DistanceAttenuatio.title: DistanceAttenuation

property/AudioEmitter/OcclusionEnabled.description:
Controls whether sound from this `Class.AudioEmitter` is muffled when
obstructed by geometry.

Controls whether occlusion (sound muffled through walls and other
geometry) is applied to this `Class.AudioEmitter` when heard by an
`Class.AudioListener`. When set to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`, the
effective value is inherited from `Class.SoundService`. When set to
`Enum.SimulationMode.Enabled` or `Enum.SimulationMode.Disabled`, it
overrides the service-level setting for this emitter.

When active, a low-pass filter is applied based on the density of
materials and thickness of obstacles between the emitter and listener.
Both the `Class.AudioEmitter` and `Class.AudioListener` must have
occlusion effectively enabled for the effect to occur on their audio path.
Disabling occlusion also disables
`Class.AudioEmitter.DiffractionEnabled|DiffractionEnabled`, since
diffraction relies on occlusion data.

Only relevant when
`Class.AudioEmitter.AcousticSimulationEnabled|AcousticSimulationEnabled`
is `true`.

Defaults to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`.
property/AudioEmitter/OcclusionEnabled.title: OcclusionEnabled

property/AudioEmitter/PositionInstance.description:
The `Class.Instance` whose position and orientation is used as the
emitter's position if `Class.AudioEmitter.PositionType|PositionType` is
set to `Enum.EmitterPositionType.Instance`.

This property is only functional when
`Class.AudioEmitter.PositionType|PositionType` is set to
`Enum.EmitterPositionType.Instance`. In that scenario, this property
determines which `Class.Instance` will be used to determine the position
of spatial audio emitted by the `Class.AudioEmitter` to be heard by
`Class.AudioListener|AudioListeners`.

If set to an instance without a position or `nil`, the
`Class.AudioEmitter` will not be heard.
property/AudioEmitter/PositionInstance.title: PositionInstance

property/AudioEmitter/PositionType.description:
Determines how the `Class.AudioEmitter` determines its 3D location.

The method by which the `Class.AudioEmitter` determines its 3D location
(the point from which audio can be heard by any nearby
`Class.AudioListener|AudioListeners`). Defaults to
`Enum.EmitterPositionType.Parent`.
property/AudioEmitter/PositionType.title: PositionType

property/AudioEmitter/ReverbEnabled.description:
Controls whether sound from this `Class.AudioEmitter` receives
environmental reverb when acoustic simulation is active.

Controls whether environmental reverberation (sound echoing off walls and
surfaces) is applied to this `Class.AudioEmitter` when heard by an
`Class.AudioListener`. When set to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`, the
effective value is inherited from `Class.SoundService`. When set to
`Enum.SimulationMode.Enabled` or `Enum.SimulationMode.Disabled`, it
overrides the service-level setting for this emitter.

When active, a reverb effect is computed from the size and material
properties of the surrounding environment. Both the `Class.AudioEmitter`
and `Class.AudioListener` must have reverb effectively enabled for the
effect to occur on their audio path.

Only relevant when
`Class.AudioEmitter.AcousticSimulationEnabled|AcousticSimulationEnabled`
is `true`.

Defaults to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`.
property/AudioEmitter/ReverbEnabled.title: ReverbEnabled

property/AudioEmitter/SimulationFidelity.description:
Controls how detailed the audio simulation should be for this
`Class.AudioEmitter`.

Controls how detailed the audio simulation should be for this
`Class.AudioEmitter`, similar to `Class.MeshPart.CollisionFidelity` or
`Class.MeshPart.RenderFidelity`.

`Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters` and
`Class.AudioListener|AudioListeners` which disagree on the necessary level
of detail will use the less-detailed option.
property/AudioEmitter/SimulationFidelity.title: SimulationFidelity

property/AudioEqualizer/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioEqualizer/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioEqualizer/HighGain.description:
Gain value to be applied to the frequency content of the highest band in
the equalizer.

Gain value, in decibels, to be applied to the frequency content of the
highest band in the equalizer. Ranges from -80 to 10.
property/AudioEqualizer/HighGain.title: HighGain

property/AudioEqualizer/LowGain.description:
Gain value to be applied to the frequency content of the lowest band in
the equalizer.

Gain value, in decibels, to be applied to the frequency content of the
lowest band in the equalizer. Ranges from -80 to 10.
property/AudioEqualizer/LowGain.title: LowGain

property/AudioEqualizer/MidGain.description:
Gain value to be applied to the frequency content of the middle band in
the equalizer.

Gain value, in decibels, to be applied to the frequency content of the
middle band in the equalizer. Ranges from -80 to 10.
property/AudioEqualizer/MidGain.title: MidGain

property/AudioEqualizer/MidRange.description:
The frequency range of the band influenced by
`Class.AudioEqualizer.MidGain|MidGain`.

The frequency range in hertz of the band influenced by
`Class.AudioEqualizer.MidGain|MidGain`. The lower value of the range
determines the crossover frequency between the low and mid bands. The
higher value of the range determines the crossover frequency between the
mid and high bands. Both crossover frequencies range from 200 to 20,000.
property/AudioEqualizer/MidRange.title: MidRange

property/AudioFader/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioFader/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioFader/Volume.description:
Volume level which is multiplied onto the input stream.

Volume level which is multiplied onto the input stream. Ranges from 0
to 3.
property/AudioFader/Volume.title: Volume

property/AudioFilter/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioFilter/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioFilter/FilterType.description:
The curve type of the band represented by the filter.

The type of frequency response curve that will be used to filter the audio
signal. Each type of curve affects the frequency content of the audio in
different ways.
property/AudioFilter/FilterType.title: FilterType

property/AudioFilter/Frequency.description:
The central frequency that the filter acts around.

The central frequency in hertz of the curve represented by the filter.
Generally, adjusting this value up or down corresponds to a horizontal
shift in the overall frequency curve. Ranges from 20 to 22000.
property/AudioFilter/Frequency.title: Frequency

property/AudioFilter/Gain.description:
For peaking and shelving filters, controls volume increase or reduction.

The gain value in decibels used to determine the volume level of the curve
represented by the filter. Only applies when the
`Class.AudioFilter|FilterType` is `Peak`, `LowShelf`, or `HighShelf`.
Ranges from -30 to 30.
property/AudioFilter/Gain.title: Gain

property/AudioFilter/Q.description:
For peaking, lowpass, highpass, bandpass, and notch filters, controls the
selectiveness or resonance.

The quality value used to determine the slope or resonance of the curve
represented by the filter. Only applies when the
`Class.AudioFilter|FilterType` is `Peak`, `Lowpass[x]dB`, `Highpass[x]dB`,
`Bandpass`, or `Notch`. Ranges from 0.1 to 10.

For `Class.AudioFilter|FilterType` values of
`Enum.AudioFilterType.Lowpass12dB|Lowpass12dB` and
`Enum.AudioFilterType.Highpass12dB|Highpass12dB`, a **Q** value of
`sqrt(2) / 2`, or `0.707`, corresponds to a flat filter at a 12dB/octave
slope.
property/AudioFilter/Q.title: Q

property/AudioFlanger/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioFlanger/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioFlanger/Depth.description:
Controls how strong the pitch modulation of the flanger is.

Controls how strong the pitch modulation of the flanger is. Ranges from
0.01 to 1 which determines the maximum delay time of the modulated signal.
A value of 1 corresponds to 10 milliseconds of maximum delay; beyond this,
the modulated signal would begin to sound more like an echo than a flange.
property/AudioFlanger/Depth.title: Depth

property/AudioFlanger/Mix.description:
Controls the balance of plain input stream to modified output stream.

Controls the balance of plain input stream to modified output stream.
Ranges from 0 to 1.
property/AudioFlanger/Mix.title: Mix

property/AudioFlanger/Rate.description:
Controls the rate of pitch modulations.

Frequency controlling the rate of pitch modulations, in hertz. Ranges from
0 to 20.
property/AudioFlanger/Rate.title: Rate

property/AudioGate/Attack.description:
Controls how long it takes for the gate to open when the signal level
rises above the `Class.AudioGate.Threshold|Threshold`.

The duration, in seconds, over which the gate will unmute the audio stream
when the signal level rises above the
`Class.AudioGate.Threshold|Threshold`. Ranges from 0.001 to 5.
property/AudioGate/Attack.title: Attack

property/AudioGate/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioGate/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioGate/Release.description:
Controls how long it takes for the gate to close when the signal level
drops below the `Class.AudioGate.Threshold|Threshold`.

The duration, in seconds, over which the gate will mute the audio stream
when the signal level drops below the
`Class.AudioGate.Threshold|Threshold`. Ranges from 0.001 to 5.
property/AudioGate/Release.title: Release

property/AudioGate/Threshold.description:
The gain value(s) around which the gate opens and closes.

The gain value(s), in decibels, at which the gate will transition from
being closed (i.e. muted) to being open (i.e. unmuted).

`Class.AudioGate.Threshold` is a `Class.NumberRange` with a "low" and a
"high" threshold. The gate starts out muted - when the input stream's
volume rises above the "high" threshold, the gate will unmute the audio
stream over the course of `Class.AudioGate.Attack|Attack` seconds. If the
input stream's volume then dips below the "low" threshold, the gate will
mute the audio stream over the course of `Class.AudioGate.Release|Release`
seconds. The two "low" and "high" thresholds create a hysteresis region to
prevent the gate from opening and closing very rapidly.

Ranges from -80 to 30, and defaults to -36 (low) and -24 (high).
property/AudioGate/Threshold.title: Threshold

property/AudioLimiter/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioLimiter/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioLimiter/MaxLevel.description:
The maximum volume tolerated.

The maximum volume, in decibels, that the limiter will allow to pass
through without reduction. Whenever the input stream exceeds
`Class.AudioLimiter.MaxLevel|MaxLevel`, the output stream's volume will be
reduced to compensate. This value ranges from `-12` to `0`.
property/AudioLimiter/MaxLevel.title: MaxLevel

property/AudioLimiter/Release.description:
The amount of time it takes for previously limited streams to return to
their normal volume.

The amount of time, in seconds, that it takes for any previously (but not
currently) limited streams to return to their normal volume. This value
ranges from `0.001` to `1`.
property/AudioLimiter/Release.title: Release

property/AudioListener/AcousticSimulatio.description:
Determines whether acoustic simulation should be used for this
`Class.AudioListener`.

Determines whether sound being heard by this `Class.AudioListener` shoud
automatically implement features of acoustic simulation, such as occlusion
(being muffled through walls), diffraction (bending around corners), and
reverberation (echoing off of walls), when being sourced from an
`Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitter`. Note that the `Class.AudioEmitter` also
needs its
`Class.AudioEmitter.AcousticSimulationEnabled|AcousticSimulationEnabled`
property set to `true` for the effects to occur.
property/AudioListener/AcousticSimulatio.title: AcousticSimulationEnabled

property/AudioListener/AngleAttenuation.description:
Represents how the perceived volume of the emitted sound changes based on
the angle between a `Class.AudioEmitter` and the
`Datatype.CFrame.LookVector|LookVector` associated with the
`Class.AudioListener`.

Represents a volume-over-angle curve that affects how loudly a
`Class.AudioListener` will hear the `Class.AudioEmitter`, based on the
angle between them and the `Datatype.CFrame.LookVector|LookVector`
associated with the `Class.AudioListener`.

This property is internal and can't be accessed by scripts; it exists to
support replication. See
`Class.AudioListener:SetAngleAttenuation()|SetAngleAttenuation()` for
usage details.
property/AudioListener/AngleAttenuation.title: AngleAttenuation

property/AudioListener/AudioInteractionG.description:
Controls which `Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters` are audible to this
`Class.AudioListener`.

Controls which `Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters` are audible to this
`Class.AudioListener`. Emitters that share an interaction group can be
heard by this Listener.
property/AudioListener/AudioInteractionG.title: AudioInteractionGroup

property/AudioListener/DiffractionEnable.description:
Controls whether sound heard by this `Class.AudioListener` bends around
corners when acoustic simulation is active.

Controls whether diffraction (sound bending around corners) is applied to
this `Class.AudioListener` when receiving audio from an
`Class.AudioEmitter`. When set to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`, the
effective value is inherited from `Class.SoundService`. When set to
`Enum.SimulationMode.Enabled` or `Enum.SimulationMode.Disabled`, it
overrides the service-level setting for this listener.

Diffraction repositions the perceived audio source to the edge of an
obstacle. Both the `Class.AudioEmitter` and `Class.AudioListener` must
have diffraction effectively enabled for the effect to occur on their
audio path. Diffraction also requires occlusion to be enabled. If
occlusion is off, sound passes straight through obstacles, so it has no
reason to bend around corners and this property has no effect. Defaults to
`Enum.SimulationMode.Default`.
property/AudioListener/DiffractionEnable.title: DiffractionEnabled

property/AudioListener/DistanceAttenuati.description:
Represents how the perceived volume of emitted sounds change as the
distance between `Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters` and the
`Class.AudioListener` increases.

Represents a volume-over-distance curve that affects how loudly the
`Class.AudioListener` hears any `Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters`, based
on the distance between them.

This property is internal and can't be accessed by scripts; it exists to
support replication. See
`Class.AudioListener:SetDistanceAttenuation()|SetDistanceAttenuation()`
for usage details.
property/AudioListener/DistanceAttenuati.title: DistanceAttenuation

property/AudioListener/OcclusionEnabled.description:
Controls whether sound heard by this `Class.AudioListener` is muffled when
obstructed by geometry.

Controls whether occlusion (sound muffled through walls and other
geometry) is applied to this `Class.AudioListener` when receiving audio
from an `Class.AudioEmitter`. When set to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`,
the effective value is inherited from `Class.SoundService`. When set to
`Enum.SimulationMode.Enabled` or `Enum.SimulationMode.Disabled`, it
overrides the service-level setting for this listener.

When active, a low-pass filter is applied based on the density of
materials and thickness of obstacles between the emitter and listener.
Both the `Class.AudioEmitter` and `Class.AudioListener` must have
occlusion effectively enabled for the effect to occur on their audio path.
Disabling occlusion also disables
`Class.AudioListener.DiffractionEnabled|DiffractionEnabled`, since
diffraction relies on occlusion data.

Defaults to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`.
property/AudioListener/OcclusionEnabled.title: OcclusionEnabled

property/AudioListener/PositionInstance.description:
The `Class.Instance` whose position and orientation is used as the
listener's position if `Class.AudioListener.PositionType|PositionType` is
set to `Enum.ListenerPositionType.Instance`.

This property is only functional when
`Class.AudioListener.PositionType|PositionType` is set to
`Enum.ListenerPositionType.Instance`. In that scenario, this property
determines which `Class.Instance` will be used to determine the position
of the `Class.AudioListener` when hearing spatial audio from
`Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters`.

If set to an instance without a position or `nil`, the
`Class.AudioListener` will not hear anything.
property/AudioListener/PositionInstance.title: PositionInstance

property/AudioListener/PositionType.description:
Determines how the `Class.AudioListener` determines its 3D location.

The method by which the `Class.AudioListener` determines its 3D location
(the point from which any nearby `Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters` can be
heard). Defaults to `Enum.ListenerPositionType.Parent`.
property/AudioListener/PositionType.title: PositionType

property/AudioListener/ReverbEnabled.description:
Controls whether sound heard by this `Class.AudioListener` receives
environmental reverb when acoustic simulation is active.

Controls whether environmental reverberation (sound echoing off walls and
surfaces) is applied to this `Class.AudioListener` when receiving audio
from an `Class.AudioEmitter`. When set to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`,
the effective value is inherited from `Class.SoundService`. When set to
`Enum.SimulationMode.Enabled` or `Enum.SimulationMode.Disabled`, it
overrides the service-level setting for this listener.

When active, a reverb effect is computed from the size and material
properties of the surrounding environment. Both the `Class.AudioEmitter`
and `Class.AudioListener` must have reverb effectively enabled for the
effect to occur on their audio path.

Defaults to `Enum.SimulationMode.Default`.
property/AudioListener/ReverbEnabled.title: ReverbEnabled

property/AudioListener/SimulationFidelit.description:
Controls how detailed the audio simulation should be for this
`Class.AudioListener`.

Controls how detailed the audio simulation should be for this
`Class.AudioListener`, similar to `Class.MeshPart.CollisionFidelity` or
`Class.MeshPart.RenderFidelity`.

`Class.AudioListener|AudioListeners` and
`Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters` which disagree on the necessary level
of detail will use the less-detailed option.
property/AudioListener/SimulationFidelit.title: SimulationFidelity

property/AudioPitchShifter/Bypass.description:
Whether audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.

If `true`, audio streams are passed-through unaffected by this effect.
property/AudioPitchShifter/Bypass.title: Bypass

property/AudioPitchShifter/Pitch.description:
Pitch modification to be multiplied by the pitch of the input stream.

Pitch modification to be multiplied by the pitch of the input stream.
Ranges from 0.5 to 2.
property/AudioPitchShifter/Pitch.title: Pitch

property/AudioPitchShifter/WindowSize.description:
Controls how much audio will be buffered and shifted at once.

Controls how much audio will be buffered and shifted at once. Larger
windows result in higher-quality pitch shifting, but introduce more
latency.
property/AudioPitchShifter/WindowSize.title: WindowSize

property/AudioPlayer/Asset.description:
The asset to be loaded into the `Class.AudioPlayer`.

The asset to be loaded into the `Class.AudioPlayer`. If
`Class.AudioPlayer.AutoLoad|AutoLoad` is `true`, the asset loads
immediately once this property is assigned. When loading is complete,
`Class.AudioPlayer.IsReady|IsReady` becomes `true`.
property/AudioPlayer/Asset.title: Asset

property/AudioPlayer/AssetId.deprecationMessage: This property is deprecated; use `Class.AudioPlayer.Asset|Asset` instead.
property/AudioPlayer/AssetId.description:
The asset to be loaded into the `Class.AudioPlayer`.

The asset to be loaded into the `Class.AudioPlayer`. If
`Class.AudioPlayer.AutoLoad|AutoLoad` is `true`, the asset loads
immediately once this property is assigned. When loading is complete,
`Class.AudioPlayer.IsReady|IsReady` becomes `true`.
property/AudioPlayer/AssetId.title: AssetId
property/AudioPlayer/AssetId.x-roblox-deprecation-message: This property is deprecated; use `Class.AudioPlayer.Asset|Asset` instead.

property/AudioPlayer/AudioContent.description:
The audio content to be loaded into the `Class.AudioPlayer`.

The audio content to be loaded into the `Class.AudioPlayer`. If
`Class.AudioPlayer.AutoLoad|AutoLoad` is `true`, the asset loads
immediately once this property is assigned. When loading is complete,
`Class.AudioPlayer.IsReady|IsReady` becomes `true`.
property/AudioPlayer/AudioContent.title: AudioContent

property/AudioPlayer/AutoLoad.description:
Controls whether `Class.AudioPlayer.Asset|Asset` loads automatically once
assigned.

Controls whether `Class.AudioPlayer.Asset|Asset` loads automatically once
assigned. If `false`, the asset will load upon the first attempt to play.
property/AudioPlayer/AutoLoad.title: AutoLoad

property/AudioPlayer/AutoPlay.description:
Denotes whether this `Class.AudioPlayer` starts playing as soon as it
spawns in for the first time.

Denotes whether this `Class.AudioPlayer` starts playing as soon as it
enters the `Class.DataModel` for the first time. This only applies to
`Class.AudioPlayer|AudioPlayers` that are created or deserialized locally,
and does not apply to `Class.AudioPlayer|AudioPlayers` generated via
replication. This property is primarily used at edit time in Studio to
have an `Class.AudioPlayer` begin when entering a play session.
property/AudioPlayer/AutoPlay.title: AutoPlay

property/AudioPlayer/IsPlaying.description:
Denotes whether this `Class.AudioPlayer` is currently playing or planning
to play.

Denotes whether this `Class.AudioPlayer` is currently playing or planning
to play. This property is read-only, but replicates. To play and stop an
`Class.AudioPlayer` at runtime, use the `Class.AudioPlayer:Play()|Play()`
and `Class.AudioPlayer:Stop()|Stop()` methods.
property/AudioPlayer/IsPlaying.title: IsPlaying

property/AudioPlayer/IsReady.description:
Denotes whether this `Class.AudioPlayer` is loaded, buffered, and ready to
play.

Denotes whether this `Class.AudioPlayer` is loaded, buffered, and ready to
play. Although uncommon, `Class.AudioPlayer|AudioPlayers` may have their
assets unloaded at runtime if there is extreme memory pressure, in which
case `Class.AudioPlayer.IsReady|IsReady` will become false.
property/AudioPlayer/IsReady.title: IsReady

property/AudioPlayer/LoopRegion.description:
A range, in seconds, denoting a desired loop start and loop end within the
`Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` of this
`Class.AudioPlayer`.

A range, in seconds, denoting a desired loop start and loop end within the
`Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` of this
`Class.AudioPlayer`.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion` minimum is **greater**
than the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` minimum, the
loop starts from the `Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion` minimum.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion` minimum is **less** than
the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` minimum, the loop
starts from the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` minimum.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion` maximum is **greater**
than the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` maximum, the
loop ends at the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion`
maximum.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion` maximum is **less** than
the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` maximum, the loop
ends at exactly the `Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion` maximum.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion` minimum **equals** the
`Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion` maximum, the `Class.AudioPlayer`
uses the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` property
instead.
property/AudioPlayer/LoopRegion.title: LoopRegion

property/AudioPlayer/Looping.description:
Controls whether this `Class.AudioPlayer` loops.

Controls whether this `Class.AudioPlayer` loops when exceeding the end of
its `Class.AudioPlayer.TimeLength|TimeLength`,
`Class.AudioPlayer.LoopRegion|LoopRegion`, or
`Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion`.
property/AudioPlayer/Looping.title: Looping

property/AudioPlayer/PlaybackRegion.description:
Range in seconds denoting a desired start time (minimum) and stop time
(maximum) within the `Class.AudioPlayer.TimeLength|TimeLength`.

Range in seconds denoting a desired start time (minimum) and stop time
(maximum) within the `Class.AudioPlayer.TimeLength|TimeLength`.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` minimum is
**greater** than 0, the sound begins playing from the
`Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` minimum time.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` minimum is
**less** than 0, the sound begins playing from 0.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` maximum is
**greater** than the `Class.AudioPlayer.TimeLength|TimeLength`, the sound
stops at `Class.AudioPlayer.TimeLength|TimeLength`.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` maximum is
**less** than the `Class.AudioPlayer.TimeLength|TimeLength`, the sound
stops at exactly the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion`
maximum.

If the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` minimum
**equals** the `Class.AudioPlayer.PlaybackRegion|PlaybackRegion` maximum,
the sound plays in its entirety.
property/AudioPlayer/PlaybackRegion.title: PlaybackRegion

property/AudioPlayer/PlaybackSpeed.description:
Controls how quickly the asset will be played, which controls its pitch.

Multiplier controlling how quickly the asset will be played, directly
controlling its perceived pitch. Ranges from 0 to 20.
property/AudioPlayer/PlaybackSpeed.title: PlaybackSpeed

property/AudioPlayer/TimeLength.description:
