Deprecated and no longer functional. Historically set whether or not
`Class.Player` character models on a team would be colored to
`Class.Team.TeamColor`.

Historically set whether or not `Class.Player` character models on a team
would be colored to `Class.Team.TeamColor`.

Developers are advised not to use this property as the script which

This property is deprecated and should not be used for new work.

team. This property offers no additional functionality and is not used by

property/Team/TeamColor.description:
This property sets the color of the `Class.Team`. Determines the
`Class.Player.TeamColor` property of players who are a member of the team.
Also determines the color displayed on the player list and above player's
heads.

This property sets the color of the `Class.Team`. Determines the
`Class.Player.TeamColor` property of players who are a member of the team.

A lot of Roblox's default team functionality is based on the team color,
rather than the name or object. For example,
`Class.SpawnLocation|SpawnLocations` can be assigned to a team via
`Class.SpawnLocation.TeamColor`. For this reason it is recommended that
developers ensure each `Class.Team` has a unique TeamColor.

Any player which is a part of a team will have their name color changed to
the team's TeamColor property. They will also be put underneath the team
heading on the player list.
property/Team/TeamColor.title: TeamColor

property/TeleportAsyncResult/PrivateServ.description:
The private server ID of the reserved server that the players are being
teleported to.

The private server ID of the reserved server that the players are being
teleported to. This field is populated only if the teleport is to a
reserved server.

This field is not the same as the private server ID of the server that
initiated the teleport, please see: `Class.DataModel.PrivateServerId`

See also:

For more information on how to teleport players between servers, see
[Teleporting Between Places](../../../projects/teleport.md).
property/TeleportAsyncResult/PrivateServ.title: PrivateServerId

property/TeleportAsyncResult/ReservedSer.description:
The access code of the reserved server that the players are being
teleported to.

The access code of the reserved server that the players are being
teleported to. This field is populated only if the teleport is to a
reserved server. This allows developers to perform subsequent teleports to
this same reserved server.

For more information on how to teleport players between servers, see
[Teleporting Between Places](../../../projects/teleport.md).
property/TeleportAsyncResult/ReservedSer.title: ReservedServerAccessCode

property/TeleportOptions/ReservedServerA.description:
The reserved server access code that indicates the reserved server that
the teleport should be to.

This property indicates the reserved server access code for the reserved
server that the user(s) should be teleported to.

The access code is obtained either from
`Class.TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync()` or from
`Class.TeleportAsyncResult.ReservedServerAccessCode`.

For more information on how to teleport players between servers, see
[Teleporting Between Places](../../../projects/teleport.md).
property/TeleportOptions/ReservedServerA.title: ReservedServerAccessCode

property/TeleportOptions/ServerInstanceI.description:
The `Class.DataModel.JobId` of the server instance to teleport to.

This property indicates the `Class.DataModel.JobId` of the server instance
the user(s) should be teleported to.

For more information on how to teleport players between servers, see
[Teleporting Between Places](../../../projects/teleport.md).
property/TeleportOptions/ServerInstanceI.title: ServerInstanceId

property/TeleportOptions/ShouldReserveSe.description:
A flag to indicate if a reserved server should be allocated and the
players should then be teleported to this allocation.

This property indicates whether the teleport call should create a new
reserved server. When set to true, a reserved server will be created and
the player(s) will be teleported to the new server.

If set to false, the player(s) will be teleported to the public server
with the specified `Class.TeleportOptions.ServerInstanceId` if provided.
When `Class.TeleportOptions.ServerInstanceId` is blank or no matching
server is found, a new public server will be created to teleport the
player(s) to.

For more information on how to teleport players between servers, see
[Teleporting Between Places](../../../projects/teleport.md).
property/TeleportOptions/ShouldReserveSe.title: ShouldReserveServer

property/TeleportService/CustomizedTelep.deprecationMessage:
This item is deprecated since the default message it controls has been
removed. Do not use it for new work.
property/TeleportService/CustomizedTelep.description:
No longer functional.

This property used to control whether or not a `Class.Message` would be
shown by default. The default message has been removed, so this no longer
does anything.
property/TeleportService/CustomizedTelep.title: CustomizedTeleportUI
property/TeleportService/CustomizedTelep.x-roblox-deprecation-message:

removed. Do not use it for new work.

property/Terrain/Decoration.description:
Enables or disables terrain decoration.

Currently enables or disables animated grass on the
`Enum.Material.Grass|Grass` terrain material, although future
modifications of this property may control additional decorative features.
property/Terrain/Decoration.title: Decoration

property/Terrain/GrassLength.description:
Specifies the length of animated grass.

Specifies the length of animated grass on the `Enum.Material.Grass|Grass`
terrain material, assuming `Class.Terrain.Decoration|Decoration` is
enabled. Valid values are between `0.1` and `1`.
property/Terrain/GrassLength.title: GrassLength

property/Terrain/IsSmooth.deprecationMessage:
The legacy terrain engine has been removed, so this property will always
be `true`.
property/Terrain/IsSmooth.description: Returns `true` if the game is using the smooth terrain system.
property/Terrain/IsSmooth.title: IsSmooth
property/Terrain/IsSmooth.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
The legacy terrain engine has been removed, so this property will always
be `true`.

property/Terrain/MaterialColors.description:
Represents the editor for the **Material Color** feature and cannot be
edited by scripts.

`MaterialColors` represents the editor for the **Material Color** feature
and cannot be edited by scripts.

To get the color of a material, use `Class.Terrain:GetMaterialColor()`. To
set the color of a material, use `Class.Terrain:SetMaterialColor()`.
property/Terrain/MaterialColors.title: MaterialColors

property/Terrain/MaxExtents.description:
Displays the boundaries of the largest possible editable region.

Displays the boundaries of the largest possible editable region as a
`Datatype.Region3int16`. The returned value spans from
`(-32000, -32000, -32000)` to `(32000, 32000, 32000)` in cell coordinates,
where each cell is 4 studs wide. This corresponds to a world-space volume
of -128,000 to 128,000 studs on each axis. The property is read-only.
property/Terrain/MaxExtents.title: MaxExtents

property/Terrain/WaterColor.description:
The tint of `Terrain` water.

The tint color applied to `Terrain` water. This `Datatype.Color3` value is
blended with the water's base appearance to shift its overall hue. The
default value is `[0.05, 0.33, 0.36]` (a dark teal).
property/Terrain/WaterColor.title: WaterColor

property/Terrain/WaterReflectance.description:
Controls how opaque `Terrain` water reflections are.

Controls how opaque the reflections on `Terrain` water are, on a scale of
`0` (no reflections) to `1` (fully opaque reflections). The default value
is `1`.
property/Terrain/WaterReflectance.title: WaterReflectance

property/Terrain/WaterTransparency.description:
The transparency of `Terrain` water.

The transparency of `Terrain` water, on a scale of `0` (fully opaque) to
`1` (fully transparent). The default value is `0.3`.
property/Terrain/WaterTransparency.title: WaterTransparency

property/Terrain/WaterWaveSize.description:
Sets the maximum height of `Terrain` water waves in studs.

Sets the maximum height of `Terrain` water waves in studs. This is
currently constrained to between `0` and `1`.
property/Terrain/WaterWaveSize.title: WaterWaveSize

property/Terrain/WaterWaveSpeed.description:
Sets how many times `Terrain` water waves will move up and down per
minute.

Sets how many times `Terrain` water waves will move up and down per
minute. This is currently constrained to between `0` and `100`.
property/Terrain/WaterWaveSpeed.title: WaterWaveSpeed

property/TerrainDetail/ColorMap.description:
Determines the color of the surface.

This property determines the color of the surface. This texture is
sometimes called the albedo texture. The alpha channel is not used.
property/TerrainDetail/ColorMap.title: ColorMap

property/TerrainDetail/ColorMapContent.description:
Determines the color of the surface. Only supports asset URIs as textures.

This property determines the color of the surface. This texture is
sometimes called the albedo texture. The alpha channel is not used.
property/TerrainDetail/ColorMapContent.title: ColorMapContent

property/TerrainDetail/EmissiveMaskConte.description:
Determines the emissivity across the surface.

This property determines the apparent emissivity across the surface. An
emissive mask is a grayscale image where black pixels correspond to no
emissivity, and white pixels correspond to full emissivity.

The emissive contribution gets added to total lighting contribution across
the surface, and the sum gets multiplied by the albedo texture, which
would be sampled from `Class.TerrainDetail.ColorMap|ColorMap` if provided.
property/TerrainDetail/EmissiveMaskConte.title: EmissiveMaskContent

property/TerrainDetail/EmissiveStrength.description:
Determines the strength of emissive contribution.

This value is a multiplier to control how strong the emissive contribution
is across the surface. If the final contribution of emissives goes beyond
supported dynamic range, it will get clamped; this could result in
emissive contribution appearing all white when using large emissive
strength values. Since this value is a multiplier, the maximum value to
prevent clamping depends on all of the other contributing values,
including `Class.TerrainDetail.EmissiveTint|EmissiveTint`,
`Class.TerrainDetail.ColorMap|ColorMap` and combined lighting
contribution.
property/TerrainDetail/EmissiveStrength.title: EmissiveStrength

property/TerrainDetail/EmissiveTint.description:
Determines the tinting color for emissive contribution.

This value is an RGB color for tinting emissive contribution.
property/TerrainDetail/EmissiveTint.title: EmissiveTint

property/TerrainDetail/Face.description:
The face this TerrainDetail overrides.

Face that this TerrainDetail overrides. When more than one TerrainDetail
objects with the same face exist under a MaterialVariant, only one of them
works.
property/TerrainDetail/Face.title: Face

property/TerrainDetail/MetalnessMap.description:
Determines which parts of the surface are metal and are non-metal.

This property determines which parts of the surface are metal and are
non-metal. A metalness map is a grayscale image where black pixels
correspond to non-metals and white pixels correspond to metals.

Metals only reflect light the same color as the metal, and they reflect
much more light than non-metals. Most materials in the real world can be
categorized either metals or non-metals. For this reason, most pixels in a
metalness map will be either pure black or pure white. Values in between
are typically used to simulate dirt or grunge on top of an underlying
metal area.

When `Class.Lighting.EnvironmentSpecularScale` is 0, metalness has no
effect. For the most realistic reflections, setting
EnvironmentSpecularScale and `Class.Lighting.EnvironmentDiffuseScale` to
1, and `Class.Lighting.Ambient` and `Class.Lighting.OutdoorAmbient` to
(0,0,0) is recommended.
property/TerrainDetail/MetalnessMap.title: MetalnessMap

property/TerrainDetail/MetalnessMapConte.description:
Determines which parts of the surface are metal and are non-metal. Only
supports asset URIs as textures.

This property determines which parts of the surface are metal and are
non-metal. A metalness map is a grayscale image where black pixels
correspond to non-metals and white pixels correspond to metals.

Metals only reflect light the same color as the metal, and they reflect
much more light than non-metals. Most materials in the real world can be
categorized either metals or non-metals. For this reason, most pixels in a
metalness map will be either pure black or pure white. Values in between
are typically used to simulate dirt or grunge on top of an underlying
metal area.

When `Class.Lighting.EnvironmentSpecularScale` is 0, metalness has no
effect. For the most realistic reflections, setting
EnvironmentSpecularScale and `Class.Lighting.EnvironmentDiffuseScale` to
1, and `Class.Lighting.Ambient` and `Class.Lighting.OutdoorAmbient` to
(0,0,0) is recommended.
property/TerrainDetail/MetalnessMapConte.title: MetalnessMapContent

property/TerrainDetail/NormalMap.description:
Modifies the lighting of the surface by adding bumps, dents, cracks, and
curves without adding more polygons.

This property modifies the lighting of the surface by adding bumps, dents,
cracks, and curves without adding more polygons.

Normal maps are RGB images that modify the surface's normal vector used
for lighting calculations. The R, G, and B channels of the NormalMap
correspond to the X, Y, and Z components of the local surface vector
respectively, and byte values of 0 and 255 for each channel correspond
linearly to normal vector components of -1 and 1.016 respectively. This
range is stretched slightly from -1 to 1 so that a byte value of 127 maps
to exactly 0. The normal vector's Z axis is always defined as the
direction of the underlying mesh's normal. A uniform (127,127,255) image
translates to a completely flat normal map where the normal is everywhere
perpendicular to the mesh surface. This format is called "tangent space"
normal maps. Roblox does not support world space or object space normal
maps.

Incorrectly flipped normal components can make bumps appear like indents.
If you import a normal map and notice the lighting looks off, you may need
to invert the G channel of the image. The X and Y axes of the tangent
space frame correspond to the X and Y directions in the image after it's
transformed by the mesh UVs. If you view your normal map in an image
editor as if it were displayed on a surface, normals pointing towards the
right side of the screen should appear more red, and normals pointing
towards the top side of your screen should appear more green.

The terms "DirectX format" and "OpenGL format" are sometimes used to
describe whether the G channel of the normal map is inverted or not.
Roblox expects the OpenGL format.

Roblox expects imported meshes to include tangents. Modeling software may
also refer to this as "tangent space" information. If you apply a normal
map and it does not seem to make any visual difference, you may need to
re-export your mesh along with its tangent information from modeling
software.
property/TerrainDetail/NormalMap.title: NormalMap

property/TerrainDetail/RoughnessMap.description:
Determines the apparent roughness across the surface.

This property determines the apparent roughness across the surface. A
roughness map is a grayscale image where black pixels correspond to a
maximally smooth surface, and white pixels correspond to a maximally rough
surface.

Roughness refers to how much variation the surface has on a very small
scale. Reflections on smooth surfaces are sharp and concentrated.
Reflections on rough surfaces are more blurry and dispersed.
property/TerrainDetail/RoughnessMap.title: RoughnessMap

property/TerrainDetail/RoughnessMapConte.description:
Determines the apparent roughness across the surface. Only supports asset
URIs as textures.

This property determines the apparent roughness across the surface. A
roughness map is a grayscale image where black pixels correspond to a
maximally smooth surface, and white pixels correspond to a maximally rough
surface.

Roughness refers to how much variation the surface has on a very small
scale. Reflections on smooth surfaces are sharp and concentrated.
Reflections on rough surfaces are more blurry and dispersed.
property/TerrainDetail/RoughnessMapConte.title: RoughnessMapContent

property/TerrainDetail/StudsPerTile.description:
Determines the scale of textures.

Determines the scale of textures. Larger values for this property will
lead to the textures appearing larger, and repeating less frequently.
property/TerrainDetail/StudsPerTile.title: StudsPerTile

This item is a deprecated function of a legacy `Class.Terrain` engine that
has been removed. Do not use it for new work.
property/TerrainRegion/IsSmooth.description:
The state of this property shows whether or not this `Class.TerrainRegion`
contains _smooth terrain_.
property/TerrainRegion/IsSmooth.title: IsSmooth
property/TerrainRegion/IsSmooth.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This item is a deprecated function of a legacy `Class.Terrain` engine that
has been removed. Do not use it for new work.

property/TerrainRegion/SizeInCells.description: The size of this TerrainRegion in cells.
property/TerrainRegion/SizeInCells.title: SizeInCells

property/TestService/AutoRuns.description:
If set to `true`, the game will start running when the service's
`Class.TestService:RunAsync()` method is called.
property/TestService/AutoRuns.title: AutoRuns

property/TestService/Description.description: A description of the test being executed.
property/TestService/Description.title: Description

property/TestService/ErrorCount.description: Measures how many errors have been recorded in the test session.
property/TestService/ErrorCount.title: ErrorCount

property/TestService/ExecuteWithStudioRu.description:
When set to `true`, `TestService` will be executed when using the **Run**
action in Roblox Studio.

When set to `true`, `TestService` will be executed when using the **Run**
action in Roblox Studio.

Note that if the `Class.TestService.NumberOfPlayers|NumberOfPlayers`
property is set to a value above `0`, running the game will open
`NumberOfPlayers + 1` Studio windows where one window is a server and the
rest are players connected to that server. Try to keep this value within a
rational range (1 to 8 players) or else your computer's CPU will get
overloaded.
property/TestService/ExecuteWithStudioRu.title: ExecuteWithStudioRun

property/TestService/Is30FpsThrottleEnab.deprecationMessage:
This has been deprecated and directly renamed to
`Class.TestService.ThrottlePhysicsToRealtime|ThrottlePhysicsToRealtime` to
better reflect its practical use.
property/TestService/Is30FpsThrottleEnab.description:
Sets whether or not the physics engine should be throttled to 30 FPS while
the test is being ran.
property/TestService/Is30FpsThrottleEnab.title: Is30FpsThrottleEnabled
property/TestService/Is30FpsThrottleEnab.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This has been deprecated and directly renamed to
`Class.TestService.ThrottlePhysicsToRealtime|ThrottlePhysicsToRealtime` to
better reflect its practical use.

property/TestService/IsPhysicsEnvironmen.description:
Sets whether or not the physics environment should be throttled while
running this test.
property/TestService/IsPhysicsEnvironmen.title: IsPhysicsEnvironmentalThrottled

property/TestService/IsSleepAllowed.description:
Sets whether or not physics objects will be allowed to fall asleep while
the test simulation is running.
property/TestService/IsSleepAllowed.title: IsSleepAllowed

property/TestService/NumberOfPlayers.description: The number of players expected in this test, if any.
property/TestService/NumberOfPlayers.title: NumberOfPlayers

property/TestService/SimulateSecondsLag.description:
Sets a specific amount of additional latency experienced by players during
the test session.
property/TestService/SimulateSecondsLag.title: SimulateSecondsLag

property/TestService/TestCount.description: Measures how many test calls have been recorded in the test session.
property/TestService/TestCount.title: TestCount

property/TestService/ThrottlePhysicsToRe.description:
Sets whether the test should be throttled to simulate time according to
real world time or as fast as possible.
property/TestService/ThrottlePhysicsToRe.title: ThrottlePhysicsToRealtime

property/TestService/Timeout.description: The maximum amount of time that tests are allowed to run for.
property/TestService/Timeout.title: Timeout

property/TestService/WarnCount.description: Measures how many warning calls have been recorded in the test session.
property/TestService/WarnCount.title: WarnCount

property/TextBox/ClearTextOnFocus.description:
Determines whether clicking on the `TextBox` will clear its
`Class.TextBox.Text` property.

Determines whether clicking on the `TextBox` will clear its
`Class.TextBox.Text` property
property/TextBox/ClearTextOnFocus.title: ClearTextOnFocus

property/TextBox/CursorPosition.description:
Determines the offset of the text cursor in bytes, or `-1` if there is no
cursor.

This property determines the offset of the text cursor in bytes, or `-1`
if the `TextBox` is not currently being edited. A value of `1` represents
the position before the first byte in the `Class.TextBox.Text|Text`
property. When used in conjunction with the
`Class.TextBox.SelectionStart|SelectionStart` property, it is possible to
both get and set selected text within a `TextBox`.

Note that the units of this property are **bytes** and that many unicode
characters such as emoji are longer than 1 byte. For instance, if a player
types in "Hello👋" ("Hello" immediately followed by the waving hand sign),
the cursor position would be `10`, not `7`, since the emoji uses 4 bytes.
property/TextBox/CursorPosition.title: CursorPosition

property/TextBox/Font.description:
Determines the font used to render text.

This property selects one of several pre-defined `Enum.Font` fonts with
which the UI element will render its text. Some fonts have bold, italic,
and/or light variants.

This property is kept in sync with the `Class.TextBox.FontFace` property.
When setting `Font`, the `Class.TextBox.FontFace|FontFace` property will
be set to `Datatype.Font.fromEnum(value)`.
property/TextBox/Font.title: Font

property/TextBox/FontFace.description:
Determines the font face used to render text.

This property is similar to the `Class.TextBox.Font|Font` property but
allows setting fonts that don't exist in `Enum.Font`.

This property is kept in sync with the `Class.TextBox.Font` property. When
setting `FontFace`, the `Class.TextBox.Font|Font` property is set to the
corresponding enum value, or to `Enum.Font.Unknown` if there are no
matches.
property/TextBox/FontFace.title: FontFace

property/TextBox/FontSize.deprecationMessage:
This item has been superseded by `Class.TextBox.TextSize` which should be
used in all new work.
property/TextBox/FontSize.description:
Determines the font size of a `TextBox` object.

This property determines the font size of a `TextBox` object.
property/TextBox/FontSize.title: FontSize
property/TextBox/FontSize.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This item has been superseded by `Class.TextBox.TextSize` which should be
used in all new work.

property/TextBox/LineHeight.description:
Scales the spacing between lines of text in the `TextBox`.

Controls the height of lines, as a multiple of the font's em square size,
by scaling the spacing between lines of text in the `TextBox`. Valid
values range from `1.0` (default) to `3.0`.
property/TextBox/LineHeight.title: LineHeight

property/TextBox/MaxVisibleGraphemes.description:
The maximum number of graphemes the `TextBox` can show.

This property controls the maximum number of graphemes (or units of text)
that are shown on the `TextBox`, regardless of whether it's showing the
`Class.TextBox.PlaceholderText|PlaceholderText` or
`Class.TextBox.Text|Text`.

Changing the property does not change the position or size of the visible
graphemes; the layout will be calculated as if all graphemes are visible.

Setting the property to `-1` disables the limit and shows the entirety of
the `Class.TextBox.Text|Text`.
property/TextBox/MaxVisibleGraphemes.title: MaxVisibleGraphemes

property/TextBox/MultiLine.description:
When set to `true`, text inside a `TextBox` is able to move onto multiple
lines.

When set to `true`, text inside a `TextBox` is able to move onto multiple
lines. This also enables players to use the <kbd>Enter</kbd> key to move
onto a new line.
property/TextBox/MultiLine.title: MultiLine

property/TextBox/PlaceholderColor3.description:
Sets the text color that gets used when no text has been entered into the
`TextBox`.
property/TextBox/PlaceholderColor3.title: PlaceholderColor3

property/TextBox/PlaceholderText.description:
Sets the text that gets displayed when no text has been entered into the
`TextBox`.
property/TextBox/PlaceholderText.title: PlaceholderText

property/TextBox/RichText.description:
Determines whether the `TextBox` renders the `Class.TextBox.Text|Text`
string using rich text formatting.

This property determines whether the `TextBox` renders the
`Class.TextBox.Text|Text` string using
[rich text](../../../ui/rich-text.md) formatting. Rich text uses simple
markup tags to style sections of the string in bold, italics, specific
colors, and more.

Note that when the `TextBox` has this property enabled and the box gains
focus, the player will be able to edit and interact with the complete XML
string, including all of the formatting tags. When focus is lost, the text
will automatically parse and render the tags as rich text.
property/TextBox/RichText.title: RichText

property/TextBox/SelectionStart.description:
Determines the starting position of a text selection.

Determines the starting position of a text selection, or `-1` if the
`TextBox` has no range of selected text. This property uses the same
positioning logic as `Class.TextBox.CursorPosition|CursorPosition`.
`SelectionStart` will be greater than
`Class.TextBox.CursorPosition|CursorPosition` if the cursor is at the
beginning of a selection, and less than
`Class.TextBox.CursorPosition|CursorPosition` if the cursor is at the end.
property/TextBox/SelectionStart.title: SelectionStart

property/TextBox/ShowNativeInput.description:
If set to `true`, input native to the platform is used instead of Roblox's
built-in keyboard.
property/TextBox/ShowNativeInput.title: ShowNativeInput

property/TextBox/Text.description:
Determines the string rendered by the `TextBox` element.

This property determines the text content rendered by the `TextBox`
element. The visual properties of the string rendered to the screen is
determined by `Class.TextBox.TextColor3|TextColor3`,
`Class.TextBox.TextTransparency|TextTransparency`,
`Class.TextBox.TextSize|TextSize`, `Class.TextBox.FontFace|FontFace`, and
other properties.

It is possible to render emoji such as 👋 and other symbols. These special
symbols aren't affected by the `Class.TextBox.TextColor3|TextColor3`
property.

This property may contain newline characters, but it is not possible to
type newline characters within the **Properties** window. Similarly, this
property may contain a tab character, but it will render as a space
instead.
property/TextBox/Text.title: Text

property/TextBox/TextBounds.description:
The size of a `TextBox` element's text in offsets.

This read-only property reflects the absolute size of rendered text in
offsets. In other words, if you were to try to fit text into a rectangle,
this property would reflect the minimum dimensions of the rectangle you
would need in order to fit the text.

Using `Class.TextService:GetTextSize()`, you can predict what `TextBounds`
will be on a `TextLabel` given a string, `Class.TextBox.Font|Font`,
`Class.TextBox.TextSize|TextSize` and frame size.
property/TextBox/TextBounds.title: TextBounds

property/TextBox/TextColor.deprecationMessage:
This item has been superseded by `Class.TextBox.TextColor3` which should
be used in all new work.
property/TextBox/TextColor.title: TextColor
property/TextBox/TextColor.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This item has been superseded by `Class.TextBox.TextColor3` which should
be used in all new work.

property/TextBox/TextColor3.description:
Determines the color of non-placeholder rendered text.

This property determines the color of non-placeholder text rendered by the
`TextBox`. Text is rendered after the text stroke.
property/TextBox/TextColor3.title: TextColor3

property/TextBox/TextEditable.description:
Determines whether the player can change the `Class.TextBox.Text|Text`.

This property determines whether the player can change the
`Class.TextBox.Text|Text` through input. It is recommended to disable
`Class.TextBox.ClearTextOnFocus|ClearTextOnFocus` when this property is
disabled, otherwise the text can be cleared on-focus.
property/TextBox/TextEditable.title: TextEditable

property/TextBox/TextFits.description: Whether the text fits within the constraints of the `TextBox`.
property/TextBox/TextFits.title: TextFits

property/TextBox/TextScaled.description:
Changes whether text is resized to fit within the `TextBox`.

This property determines whether text is scaled so that it fills the box's
entire space. When enabled, `Class.TextBox.TextSize|TextSize` is ignored
and `Class.TextBox.TextWrapped|TextWrapped` is automatically enabled. When
this property is used for on-screen UI, it may be helpful to use a
`Class.UITextSizeConstraint` to restrict the range of possible text sizes.

See `Class.TextLabel.TextScaled` for additional recommendations when using
this property.
property/TextBox/TextScaled.title: TextScaled

property/TextBox/TextSize.description:
Determine the line height of text in offsets.

This property determines the height in offsets of one line of rendered
text. The unit is in offsets, not points as in many document editing
programs.
property/TextBox/TextSize.title: TextSize

property/TextBox/TextStrokeColor3.description:
Determines the color of the text stroke (outline).

This property sets the color of the stroke (outline) of the rendered text.
This property and
`Class.TextBox.TextStrokeTransparency|TextStrokeTransparency` determine
the visual appearance of the text stroke.
property/TextBox/TextStrokeColor3.title: TextStrokeColor3

property/TextBox/TextStrokeTransparency.description:
Determines the transparency of the text stroke (outline).

This property sets the transparency of the stroke (outline) of the
rendered text. This property and
`Class.TextBox.TextStrokeColor3|TextStrokeColor3` determine the visual
appearance of the text stroke.

Since text stroke is simply multiple renderings of the same transparency,
this property is essentially multiplicative on itself four times over; for
example a `TextStrokeTransparency` of `0.5` appears about the same as
`Class.TextBox.TextTransparency|TextTransparency` of `0.0625`, or `0.5^4`.
property/TextBox/TextStrokeTransparency.title: TextStrokeTransparency

property/TextBox/TextTransparency.description:
Determines the transparency of the rendered text.

This property determines the transparency of all the text rendered by the
`TextBox`.
property/TextBox/TextTransparency.title: TextTransparency

property/TextBox/TextTruncate.description: Controls the truncation of the text displayed in the `TextBox`.
property/TextBox/TextTruncate.title: TextTruncate

property/TextBox/TextWrap.deprecationMessage:
This item has been superseded by `Class.TextBox.TextWrapped` which should
be used in all new work.
property/TextBox/TextWrap.title: TextWrap
property/TextBox/TextWrap.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This item has been superseded by `Class.TextBox.TextWrapped` which should
be used in all new work.

property/TextBox/TextWrapped.description:
Determines if text wraps to multiple lines within the `TextBox` element
space, truncating excess text.

When enabled, this property will render text on multiple lines within a
`TextBox` element's space so that `Class.TextBox.TextBounds|TextBounds`
will never exceed the `Class.GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize` of the element.

This is achieved by breaking long lines of text into multiple lines. Line
breaks will prefer whitespace; should a long unbroken word exceed the
width of the element, that word will be broken into multiple lines.

If further line breaks would cause the vertical height of the text (the

`Class.TextButton.TextTransparency|TextTransparency`,
`Class.TextButton.TextSize|TextSize`, `Class.TextButton.Font|Font`,
`Class.TextButton.TextScaled|TextScaled`,
`Class.TextButton.TextWrapped|TextWrapped`,
`Class.TextButton.TextXAlignment|TextXAlignment` and
`Class.TextButton.TextYAlignment|TextYAlignment`.

It is possible to render emoji such as 🔒 and other symbols which aren't
affected by the `Class.TextButton.TextColor3|TextColor3` property. These
can be pasted into `Class.Script` and `Class.LocalScript` objects, as well
as the field within the [Properties](../../../studio/properties.md)
window.

This property may contain newline characters. Similarly, this property may
contain a tab character, but it will render as a space instead.

property/TextButton/TextScaled.description:
Changes whether text is resized to fit within the `Class.TextButton`.

This property determines whether text is scaled so that it fills the
button's entire space. When enabled, `Class.TextButton.TextSize|TextSize`
is ignored and `Class.TextButton.TextWrapped|TextWrapped` is automatically
enabled. This property is useful for rendering text elements within
`Class.BillboardGui|BillboardGuis`. When this property is used for
[on-screen UI](../../../ui/on-screen-containers.md), it may be helpful to
use a `Class.UITextSizeConstraint` to restrict the range of possible text
sizes.

##### Automatic Sizing

It's recommended that you avoid usage of
`Class.TextButton.TextScaled|TextScaled` and adjust UI to take advantage
of the `Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` property instead.
Here are the core differences between the two properties:

- `Class.TextButton.TextScaled|TextScaled` scales the content (text) to
  accommodate the UI. Without careful consideration, some text may become
  unreadable if scaled too small.

- `Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` resizes the UI to
  accommodate content while maintaining a consistent font size. For more
  information, see [here](../../../ui/size-modifiers.md#automatic-sizing).

Additionally, it's recommended that you avoid applying both
`Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` and
`Class.TextButton.TextScaled|TextScaled` and to the same
`Class.TextButton`. `Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize`
determines the maximum amount of available space that a `Class.GuiObject`
can use (in this case, text), while
`Class.TextButton.TextScaled|TextScaled` uses the available space
determined by `Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` to scale the
font size up to the maximum font size (100) if there are no size
constraints.

property/TextButton/TextStrokeTransparen.description:
Determines the transparency of the text stroke (outline).

This property sets the transparency of the stroke, or outline, of rendered
text. Along with `Class.TextButton.TextStrokeColor3|TextStrokeColor3`, it
determines the final visual appearance of the text stroke.

Note that text stroke is multiple renderings of the same transparency, so
this property is essentially multiplicative on itself four times over.
Therefore, it's recommended to set
`Class.TextButton.TextStrokeTransparency|TextStrokeTransparency` to a
value in the range of `0.75` to `1` for more a more subtle effect.

As a powerful alternative which supports color gradients, see

property/TextChatMessage/Metadata.description:
A general purpose field for storing miscellaneous data about the `Class.TextChatMessage`. A general purpose field for storing miscellaneous data about the `TextChatMessage`. The second argument of `Class.TextChannel:SendAsync()` and `Class.TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage()` is used to populate this field. Use this field to apply additional formatting for special messages within `Class.TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage` and `Class.TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage` callbacks. ```lua local Players = game:GetService("Players") local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService") local customChannel: TextChannel = Instance.new("TextChannel") customChannel.Parent = TextChatService:WaitForChild("TextChannels") customChannel.OnIncomingMessage = function(message: TextChatMessage) if string.find(message.Metadata, "Error") then local overrideProperties = Instance.new("TextChatMessageProperties") overrideProperties.Text = string.format("%s", message.Text) return overrideProperties elseif string.find(message.Metadata, "Info") then local overrideProperties = Instance.new("TextChatMessageProperties") overrideProperties.Text = string.format("%s", message.Text) return overrideProperties end return nil end Players.LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded:Connect(function() customChannel:DisplaySystemMessage("This is an error!", "Game.Error.Generic") customChannel:DisplaySystemMessage("Could not find save data!", "Game.Error.SaveDataNotFound") customChannel:DisplaySystemMessage("You won the game!", "Game.Info.Win") customChannel:DisplaySystemMessage("You lost the game!", "Game.Info.Lose") end) ``` As follows is a reference of the default system messages emitted by the chat system:

property/TextChatService/CreateDefaultCo.description:
Determines whether `Class.TextChatService` should create default `Class.TextChatCommand|TextChatCommands`. Determines whether `Class.TextChatService` should create default `Class.TextChatCommand|TextChatCommands`. If `true`, the following `Class.TextChatCommand|TextChatCommands` are created and put in a `Class.Folder` named **TextChatCommands** inside `Class.TextChatService`:
Name Primary Alias Secondary Alias Description Usage Example
RBXClearCommand clear cls Clears the chat log for the local user. /cls
RBXConsoleCommand console Opens the Developer Console. /console
RBXEmoteCommand emote e Plays an avatar emote. /e dance
RBXHelpCommand help ? Shows a list of chat commands. /help
RBXMuteCommand mute m Mutes a user by their Class.Player.Name|Name or Class.Player.DisplayName|DisplayName in all Class.TextChannel|TextChannels. /m Username
RBXTeamCommand team t Enters team chat mode where messages are only visible to teammates. /t
RBXUnmuteCommand unmute um Unmutes a user by their Class.Player.Name|Name or Class.Player.DisplayName|DisplayName in all Class.TextChannel|TextChannels. /um Username
RBXVersionCommand version v Shows the chat version. /version
RBXWhisperCommand whisper w Enters whisper mode with another Class.Player. /w DisplayName or /w @Username
Note that you can edit, create, and remove `Class.TextChatCommand|TextChatCommands` even if `Class.TextChatService.CreateDefaultCommands|CreateDefaultCommands` is `true`. Also note that mute and unmute commands apply to all `Class.TextChannel|TextChannels`.
property/TextChatService/CreateDefaultCo.title: CreateDefaultCommands

property/TextChatService/CreateDefaultTe.description:
Determines whether `Class.TextChatService` should create default `Class.TextChannel|TextChannels`. Determines whether `Class.TextChatService` should create default `Class.TextChannel|TextChannels`. If `true`, a `Class.Folder` named **TextChannels** is created inside `Class.TextChatService` at runtime to contain the `Class.TextChannel|TextChannels` outlined in the table below. Each of the default channels has the described special behavior applied to messages using its internally bound `Class.TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage` callback function, changing how messages appear when sent through the channel. The callback is assigned automatically either at runtime (if the `Class.TextChannel` exists) or when the `Class.TextChannel` is created.
Channel Description
RBXGeneral Class.TextChannel for player messages. In the chat window, messages are modified such that Class.TextChatMessage.PrefixText|PrefixText receives a rich text font color tag to give chatting players their distinctive name color. If Class.Player.Team exists, that Class.Team.TeamColor is used instead of the default name color.
RBXSystem Class.TextChannel for system messages. In the chat window, messages are modified such that Class.TextChatMessage.Text is given a light grey color tag by default, or a red color tag if Class.TextChatMessage.Metadata contains the word "Error".
RBXTeam[BrickColor] Class.TextChannel for team-specific player messages, created when a Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor is in use by any Class.Team within the Class.Teams service. Name of the created channel is RBXTeam followed by the Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor name. For example, RBXTeamCrimson is a Class.TextChannel created when there is an active team whose Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor property is the "Crimson" Datatype.BrickColor.

In the chat window, messages are modified such that Class.TextChatMessage.PrefixText|PrefixText is colored according to the Class.Player.TeamColor|TeamColor and is prepended with [Team].

Team channels create Class.TextSource|TextSources for all non‑Class.Player.Neutral|Neutral players with the matching Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor, allowing them to use team‑only chat. Channels are removed if there are no remaining teams with an associated Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor.
RBXWhisper:[UserId1]_[UserId2] Class.TextChannel for whisper messages between two players, created when a player uses the /whisper command on another player. For example RBXWhisper:2276836_505306092 is a Class.TextChannel for players with Class.Player.UserId|UserIds 2276836 and 505306092. Inside whisper channels are two Class.TextSource|TextSources associated with the respective Class.Player.UserId|UserIds.

In the chat window, messages are colored the same as those in RBXGeneral and Class.TextChatMessage.PrefixText is modified to show whether a message was sent from or received by the local user.

Whisper channels are removed when either player leaves the experience.
Note that the default `Class.TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage` callbacks can be overwritten. Also note that you can edit, create, and remove `Class.TextChannel|TextChannels` even if `Class.TextChatService.CreateDefaultTextChannels|CreateDefaultTextChannels` is `true`. Messages from different TextChannels can be separated into different tabs in the chat window using `Class.ChannelTabsConfiguration`.
property/TextChatService/CreateDefaultTe.title: CreateDefaultTextChannels

property/TextFilterTranslatedResult/Sour.description:
The language of the original text that was filtered.

The language string of the original text that was submitted to
`Class.TextService:FilterAndTranslateStringAsync()`. This is the source
language that the translations returned by
`Class.TextFilterTranslatedResult:GetTranslations()` were translated from.
This property is read-only.
property/TextFilterTranslatedResult/Sour.title: SourceLanguage

property/TextFilterTranslatedResult/Sour.description:
The filtered form of the original, untranslated text.

A `Class.TextFilterResult` representing the filtered form of the original
text that was submitted to
`Class.TextService:FilterAndTranslateStringAsync()`, in its
`Class.TextFilterTranslatedResult.SourceLanguage`. Use the returned
`Class.TextFilterResult` to obtain the correctly filtered string for each
recipient before displaying the untranslated text. This property is
read-only.
property/TextFilterTranslatedResult/Sour.title: SourceText

property/TextGenerator/Seed.description:
Sets a fixed seed for the random number generator, allowing reproducible
responses in cases where the same input parameters are used across
multiple requests.

Sets a fixed seed for the random number generator, allowing reproducible
responses in cases where the same input parameters are used across
multiple requests. By setting the same seed value, you can obtain
identical results for debugging, testing, or evaluation purposes. The
value of `Seed` should be an integer. Non-integral values will be
truncated. Default is `0`.
property/TextGenerator/Seed.title: Seed

property/TextGenerator/SystemPrompt.description:
Provides context to the model about its role, tone, or behavior during
conversation.

Provides context to the model about its role, tone, or behavior during the
conversation. This parameter can guide the model on how to respond,
setting expectations like `"You are an assistant"` or
`"Use a formal tone"`.
property/TextGenerator/SystemPrompt.title: SystemPrompt

property/TextGenerator/Temperature.description:
Controls the "creativity" or randomness of the model's responses.

Controls the "creativity" or randomness of the model's responses. Values
closer to `1` increase randomness, while values closer to `0` make the
responses more focused and deterministic. Values outside the accepted
range are clamped to the range of `[0.4, 1.0]`. Default is `0.7`.
property/TextGenerator/Temperature.title: Temperature

property/TextGenerator/TopP.description:
Helps the AI model narrow or expand the range of possible words to sample
from while generating the next token.

Helps the model narrow or expand the range of possible words to sample
from while generating the next token. This setting narrows the token
choices to only contain words that together make up a certain percentage
of total likelihood (for example, 90%). A lower `TopP` means the model
sticks to closer and more predictable choices, while a higher `TopP` opens
the door to more diverse and creative responses. Values outside the
accepted range are clamped to the range of `[0.5, 1.0]`. Default is `0.9`.
property/TextGenerator/TopP.title: TopP

property/TextLabel/ContentText.description:
A copy of `Class.TextLabel.Text` that contains exactly what is being rendered by the `Class.TextLabel`. This property provides a copy of `Class.TextLabel.Text|Text` that contains exactly what is being rendered by the `Class.TextLabel`. This is useful for eliminating style tags used for [rich text](../../../ui/rich-text.md) markup; for example, when `Class.TextLabel.RichText|RichText` is enabled, the `Class.TextLabel.ContentText|ContentText` property shows the text as it appears to the user.
RichText Text ContentText
false <b>Hello,<br/> world!</b> <b>Hello,<br/> world!</b>
true <b>Hello,<br/> world!</b> Hello,
world!
property/TextLabel/ContentText.title: ContentText

property/TextLabel/Font.description:
Determines the font used to render text.

This property selects one of several pre-defined fonts with which the
`Class.TextLabel` will render its text. Some fonts have bold, italic
and/or light variants.

With the exception of the `Enum.Font.Legacy` font, each font will render
text with the line height equal to the `Class.TextLabel.TextSize|TextSize`
property.

The `Enum.Font.Code` font is the only monospace font. It has the unique
property that each character has the exact same width and height ratio of
1:2, where the width of each character is approximately half the
`Class.TextLabel.TextSize|TextSize` property.

This property is kept in sync with the `Class.TextLabel.FontFace|FontFace`
property.
property/TextLabel/Font.title: Font

property/TextLabel/FontFace.description:
Determines the font used to render text.

This property is similar to the `Class.TextLabel.Font|Font` property but
allows setting fonts that don't exist in `Enum.Font`.

This property is kept in sync with the `Class.TextLabel.Font|Font`
property, such that when setting `Class.TextLabel.FontFace|FontFace`, the
font is set to the corresponding `Enum.Font` value or to
`Enum.Font.Unknown` if there are no matches.
property/TextLabel/FontFace.title: FontFace

property/TextLabel/FontSize.deprecationMessage:
This property is deprecated in favor of `Class.TextLabel|TextSize` which
is an integer and not an enum and thus offers far more options for sizes.
property/TextLabel/FontSize.description:
Determines the font size to be used.

This property determines the font size to be used.
property/TextLabel/FontSize.title: FontSize
property/TextLabel/FontSize.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This property is deprecated in favor of `Class.TextLabel|TextSize` which
is an integer and not an enum and thus offers far more options for sizes.

property/TextLabel/LineHeight.description:
Scales the spacing between lines of text in the `Class.TextLabel`.

Controls the height of lines as a multiple of the font's `em` square size
by scaling the spacing between lines of text in the `Class.TextLabel`.
Valid values range from `1.0` to `3.0`, defaulting to `1.0`.
property/TextLabel/LineHeight.title: LineHeight

property/TextLabel/LocalizedText.description:
Read-only string containing the automatically-localized text that the
`Class.TextLabel` renders.

This read-only property holds the automatically-localized text that the
`Class.TextLabel` renders. When automatic localization is enabled through
`Class.GuiBase2d.AutoLocalize|AutoLocalize` and the label's
`Class.TextLabel.Text|Text` matches an entry in an applicable localization
table for the player's locale, this property contains the translated
string that is actually displayed; when no translation applies, it falls
back to the label's own text. It defaults to an empty string and can't be
set from a script.
property/TextLabel/LocalizedText.title: LocalizedText

property/TextLabel/MaxVisibleGraphemes.description:
The maximum number of graphemes the `Class.TextLabel` can show.

This property controls the maximum number of graphemes (or units of text)
that are shown on the `Class.TextLabel`. It is primarily provided as an
easy way to create a
[typewriter effect](../../../ui/animation.md#typewriter-effect) where the
characters appear one at a time.

Changing the property does not change the position or size of the visible
graphemes; the layout will be calculated as if all graphemes are visible.

Setting the property to `-1` disables the limit and shows the entirety of
the `Class.TextLabel.Text|Text`.
property/TextLabel/MaxVisibleGraphemes.title: MaxVisibleGraphemes

property/TextLabel/OpenTypeFeatures.description:
Applies OpenType typographic features to the text rendered by the
`Class.TextLabel`.

This property is a comma-separated list of OpenType feature tags that are
applied when the `Class.TextLabel` shapes and renders its text, such as
`zero` for slashed zeros or `ss03` for a stylistic set. It defaults to an
empty string, which applies no additional features.

Each entry uses the standard OpenType feature-string syntax (for example,
`zero` or `ss03`). Only a supported subset of features is applied; a
feature that isn't supported, a malformed string, or the bracketed
partial-enabling syntax (for example, `zero[1:3]`) is rejected, and the
reason is reported through
`Class.TextLabel.OpenTypeFeaturesError|OpenTypeFeaturesError`.

This property supports [styling](../../../ui/styling/index.md).
property/TextLabel/OpenTypeFeatures.title: OpenTypeFeatures

property/TextLabel/OpenTypeFeaturesError.description:
Read-only property that describes why the
`Class.TextLabel.OpenTypeFeatures` string could not be applied.

This read-only property reports the error, if any, encountered while
parsing and applying the
`Class.TextLabel.OpenTypeFeatures|OpenTypeFeatures` string. It defaults to
an empty string, which indicates that the requested features were applied
successfully.

When a feature can't be applied, this property is set to one of the
following messages:

- `Failed to parse features.` when a feature string is malformed.
- `Unsupported feature: <tag>` when a feature isn't part of the supported
  set.
- `Partial feature enabling not supported.` when the string uses the
  bracketed range syntax.
property/TextLabel/OpenTypeFeaturesError.title: OpenTypeFeaturesError

property/TextLabel/RichText.description:
Determines whether the `Class.TextLabel` renders its text using rich text
formatting.

This property determines whether the `Class.TextLabel` renders its text
using [rich text](../../../ui/rich-text.md) markup to style sections of
the string in bold, italics, specific colors, and more.

To use rich text, simply include rich text formatting tags in the
`Class.TextLabel.Text|Text` string.
property/TextLabel/RichText.title: RichText

property/TextLabel/Text.description:
Determines the string rendered by the `Class.TextLabel`.

This property determines the text content rendered by the
`Class.TextLabel`. The visual properties of the string rendered to the
screen is determined by `Class.TextLabel.TextColor3|TextColor3`,
`Class.TextLabel.TextTransparency|TextTransparency`,
`Class.TextLabel.TextSize|TextSize`, `Class.TextLabel.Font|Font`,
`Class.TextLabel.TextScaled|TextScaled`,
`Class.TextLabel.TextWrapped|TextWrapped`,
`Class.TextLabel.TextXAlignment|TextXAlignment` and
`Class.TextLabel.TextYAlignment|TextYAlignment`.

It is possible to render emoji such as 🔒 and other symbols which aren't
affected by the `Class.TextLabel.TextColor3|TextColor3` property. These
can be pasted into `Class.Script` and `Class.LocalScript` objects, as well
as the field within the [Properties](../../../studio/properties.md)
window.

This property may contain newline characters. Similarly, this property may
contain a tab character, but it will render as a space instead.
property/TextLabel/Text.title: Text

property/TextLabel/TextBounds.description:
Read-only property which reflects the absolute size of rendered text in

This read-only property reflects the absolute size of rendered text in
offsets, meaning that if you try to fit text into a rectangle, this
property would reflect the minimum dimensions of the rectangle you'd need
in order to fit the text.

Using `Class.TextService:GetTextSize()`, you can predict what
`Class.TextLabel.TextBounds|TextBounds` will be given a string,
`Class.TextLabel.Font|Font`, `Class.TextLabel.TextSize|TextSize`, and
frame size.
property/TextLabel/TextBounds.title: TextBounds

property/TextLabel/TextColor.deprecationMessage:
This item has been superseded by `Class.TextLabel.TextColor3` which should
be used in all new work.
property/TextLabel/TextColor.description:
Determines the color of text.

This property determines the color of text.
property/TextLabel/TextColor.title: TextColor
property/TextLabel/TextColor.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This item has been superseded by `Class.TextLabel.TextColor3` which should
be used in all new work.

property/TextLabel/TextColor3.description:
Determines the color of rendered text.

This property determines the color of all the text rendered by the
`Class.TextLabel` element.
property/TextLabel/TextColor3.title: TextColor3

property/TextLabel/TextDirection.description:
Direction in which the text is rendered.

This property sets the base direction in which the `Class.TextLabel`
orders and renders its text, using a value of the `Enum.TextDirection`
enum. It defaults to `Enum.TextDirection.Auto`, which infers the direction
from the content of `Class.TextLabel.Text|Text` so that left-to-right and
right-to-left scripts are ordered correctly. Set it to
`Enum.TextDirection.LeftToRight` or `Enum.TextDirection.RightToLeft` to
force a specific direction regardless of the text content.

This property supports [styling](../../../ui/styling/index.md).
property/TextLabel/TextDirection.title: TextDirection

property/TextLabel/TextFits.description:
A boolean representation of whether the label's text fits within the size
of it.

This read-only property is `true` when the text rendered by the
`Class.TextLabel` fits entirely within the element's
`Class.GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize`, and `false` when the text is too large and
is therefore clipped or truncated. It's computed from
`Class.TextLabel.TextBounds|TextBounds` relative to the available space,
so it reflects the combined effect of
`Class.TextLabel.TextWrapped|TextWrapped`,
`Class.TextLabel.TextTruncate|TextTruncate`, and
`Class.TextLabel.TextScaled|TextScaled`.
property/TextLabel/TextFits.title: TextFits

property/TextLabel/TextScaled.description:
Changes whether text is resized to fit within the `Class.TextLabel`.

This property determines whether text is scaled so that it fills the
label's entire space. When enabled, `Class.TextLabel.TextSize|TextSize` is
ignored and `Class.TextLabel.TextWrapped|TextWrapped` is automatically
enabled. This property is useful for rendering text elements within
`Class.BillboardGui|BillboardGuis`. When this property is used for
[on-screen UI](../../../ui/on-screen-containers.md), it may be helpful to
use a `Class.UITextSizeConstraint` to restrict the range of possible text
sizes.

##### Automatic Sizing

It's recommended that you avoid usage of
`Class.TextLabel.TextScaled|TextScaled` and adjust UI to take advantage of
the `Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` property instead. Here
are the core differences between the two properties:

- `Class.TextLabel.TextScaled|TextScaled` scales the content (text) to
  accommodate the UI. Without careful consideration, some text may become
  unreadable if scaled too small.

- `Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` resizes the UI to
  accommodate content while maintaining a consistent font size. For more
  information, see [here](../../../ui/size-modifiers.md#automatic-sizing).

Additionally, it's recommended that you avoid applying both
`Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` and
`Class.TextLabel.TextScaled|TextScaled` and to the same `Class.TextLabel`.
`Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` determines the maximum
amount of available space that a `Class.GuiObject` can use (in this case,
text), while `Class.TextLabel.TextScaled|TextScaled` uses the available
space determined by `Class.GuiObject.AutomaticSize|AutomaticSize` to scale
the font size up to the maximum font size (100) if there are no size
constraints.
property/TextLabel/TextScaled.title: TextScaled

property/TextLabel/TextSize.description:
Determines the line height of text in offsets.

This property determines the height of one line of rendered text. The unit
is in offsets, not points (which is used in most document editing
programs). The `Enum.Font.Legacy` font does not hold this property.
property/TextLabel/TextSize.title: TextSize

property/TextLabel/TextStrokeColor3.description:
Determines the color of the text stroke (outline).

This property sets the color of the stroke, or outline, of rendered text.
Along with
`Class.TextLabel.TextStrokeTransparency|TextStrokeTransparency`, it
determines the final visual appearance of the text stroke.

As a powerful alternative which supports color gradients, see
`Class.UIStroke`.
property/TextLabel/TextStrokeColor3.title: TextStrokeColor3

property/TextLabel/TextStrokeTransparenc.description:
Determines the transparency of the text stroke (outline).

This property sets the transparency of the stroke, or outline, of rendered
text. Along with `Class.TextLabel.TextStrokeColor3|TextStrokeColor3`, it
determines the final visual appearance of the text stroke.

Note that text stroke is multiple renderings of the same transparency, so
this property is essentially multiplicative on itself four times over.
Therefore, it's recommended to set
`Class.TextLabel.TextStrokeTransparency|TextStrokeTransparency` to a value
in the range of `0.75` to `1` for more a more subtle effect.

As a powerful alternative which supports color gradients, see
`Class.UIStroke`.
property/TextLabel/TextStrokeTransparenc.title: TextStrokeTransparency

property/TextLabel/TextTransparency.description:
Determines the transparency of rendered text.

This property determines the transparency of all the text rendered by the
`Class.TextLabel`.
property/TextLabel/TextTransparency.title: TextTransparency

property/TextLabel/TextTruncate.description:
Controls the truncation of the text displayed in the `Class.TextLabel`.

This property controls how the `Class.TextLabel` truncates text that is
too large to fit within the element, using a value of the
`Enum.TextTruncate` enum. It defaults to `Enum.TextTruncate.None`, which
leaves text untruncated. `Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd` truncates at word
boundary and replaces the overflowing graphemes with an ellipsis (`...`),
respecting word boundaries where possible, while
`Enum.TextTruncate.SplitWord` truncates inside a word when the line ends
in the middle of one.

This property supports [styling](../../../ui/styling/index.md).
property/TextLabel/TextTruncate.title: TextTruncate

property/TextLabel/TextWrap.deprecationMessage:
This property is simply an alias for `Class.TextLabel|TextWrapped`. Use
the past-tense version instead.
property/TextLabel/TextWrap.description:
Determines whether or not text should wrap at the edges of the
`Class.TextLabel` element's space.

This property determines whether or not text should wrap at the edges of
the `Class.TextLabel` element's space.
property/TextLabel/TextWrap.title: TextWrap
property/TextLabel/TextWrap.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This property is simply an alias for `Class.TextLabel|TextWrapped`. Use
the past-tense version instead.

property/TextLabel/TextWrapped.description:
Determines if text wraps to multiple lines within the `Class.TextLabel`

When enabled, this property will render text on multiple lines within a
`Class.TextLabel` element's space so that
`Class.TextLabel.TextBounds|TextBounds` will never exceed the
`Class.GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize` of the element. This is achieved by
breaking long lines of text into multiple lines.

Line breaks will prefer whitespace; should a long unbroken word exceed the
width of the element, that word will be broken into multiple lines.

If further line breaks would cause the vertical height of the text (the
**Y** component of `Class.TextLabel.TextBounds|TextBounds`) to exceed the
vertical height of the element (the **Y** component of
`Class.GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize`), then that line will not be rendered at
all.
property/TextLabel/TextWrapped.title: TextWrapped

property/TextLabel/TextXAlignment.description:
Determines the horizontal alignment of rendered text.

This property determines the horizontal alignment of text rendered within
the object's space. It is used in conjunction with
`Class.TextLabel.TextYAlignment|TextYAlignment` to fully determine text
alignment on both axes.

Note that this property won't affect the read-only properties
`Class.TextLabel.TextBounds|TextBounds` and
`Class.TextLabel.TextFits|TextFits`.
property/TextLabel/TextXAlignment.title: TextXAlignment

property/TextLabel/TextYAlignment.description:
Determines the vertical alignment of rendered text.

This property determines the vertical alignment of text rendered within
the object's space. It is used in conjunction with
`Class.TextLabel.TextXAlignment|TextXAlignment` to fully determine text
alignment on both axes.

Note that this property won't affect the read-only properties
`Class.TextLabel.TextBounds|TextBounds` and
`Class.TextLabel.TextFits|TextFits`.
property/TextLabel/TextYAlignment.title: TextYAlignment

property/TextSource/CanSend.description:
Determines whether the user can send messages to the `Class.TextChannel`.

Determines whether the user can send messages to the `Class.TextChannel`.

If `false`, user can only read messages in the `Class.TextChannel`.
property/TextSource/CanSend.title: CanSend

property/TextSource/UserId.description:
UserId of the user represented by the `Class.TextSource`.

UserId of the user represented by the `Class.TextSource`.

Support for non-user entities may be added in the future via passing in
negative numbers for this property.
property/TextSource/UserId.title: UserId

property/Texture/OffsetStudsU.description:
Determines the offset in studs of the rendered texture's horizontal
coordinate.

This property determines how far the rendered texture is offset on the
horizontal axis, in studs, as visualized
[here](../../../parts/textures-decals.md#offset-textures).

See also `Class.Texture.OffsetStudsV|OffsetStudsV`.
property/Texture/OffsetStudsU.title: OffsetStudsU

property/Texture/OffsetStudsV.description:
Determines the offset in studs of the rendered texture's vertical
coordinate.

This property determines how far the rendered texture is offset on the
vertical axis, in studs, as visualized
[here](../../../parts/textures-decals.md#offset-textures).

See also `Class.Texture.OffsetStudsU|OffsetStudsU`.
property/Texture/OffsetStudsV.title: OffsetStudsV

property/Texture/StudsPerTileU.description:
Sets the horizontal size, in studs, of the tiled image applied by the
`Class.Texture`.

Sets the horizontal size, in studs, of the tiled image applied by the
`Class.Texture`.

Larger values for this property will lead to the `Class.Texture` appearing
larger, and repeating less frequently. Unlike with `Class.Decal|Decals`,
the size of the repeated image is unaffected by the dimensions of the
`Class.BasePart`. Instead, resizing the `Class.BasePart` only increases
the number of times the texture repeats.

Note that this property can be set to very low values, but not zero. Also
note that the horizontal/vertical distinction is relative to the parent
`Class.BasePart` axis; therefore the `Class.Texture` will rotate along
with the `Class.BasePart`.

See also `Class.Texture.StudsPerTileV|StudsPerTileV`.
property/Texture/StudsPerTileU.title: StudsPerTileU

property/Texture/StudsPerTileV.description:
Sets the vertical size, in studs, of the tiled image applied by the
`Class.Texture`.

Sets the vertical size, in studs, of the tiled image applied by the
`Class.Texture`.

Larger values for this property will lead to the `Class.Texture` appearing
larger, and repeating less frequently. Unlike with `Class.Decal|Decals`,
the size of the repeated image is unaffected by the dimensions of the
`Class.BasePart`. Instead, resizing the `Class.BasePart` only increases
the number of times the texture repeats.

Note that this property can be set to very low values, but not zero. Also
note that the horizontal/vertical distinction is relative to the parent
`Class.BasePart` axis; therefore the `Class.Texture` will rotate along
with the `Class.BasePart`.

See also `Class.Texture.StudsPerTileU|StudsPerTileU`.
property/Texture/StudsPerTileV.title: StudsPerTileV

property/Tool/CanBeDropped.description:
Controls whether the player can drop the tool.

The CanBeDropped property controls whether the player can drop the
`Class.Tool`.

If true, when the backspace button is pressed, the tool will be parented
to `Class.Workspace` and removed from the player's `Class.Backpack`. If
false, nothing will happen when backspace is pressed, and the tool will
remain equipped.
property/Tool/CanBeDropped.title: CanBeDropped

property/Tool/Enabled.description:
Relates to whether or not the tool can be used.

The **Enabled** property relates to whether or not the `Class.Tool` can be
used. This is useful if you want to prevent a player from using a tool,
but don't want to remove it from their `Class.Backpack`.

When set to `true`, the player can use the tool. When set to `false`, the
tool is disabled and the player cannot use it; this prevents the tool from
being activated or deactivated by the `Class.Tool:Activate()` and
`Class.Tool:Deactivate()` methods, and it prevents the
`Class.Tool.Activated` and `Class.Tool.Deactivated` events from firing.
property/Tool/Enabled.title: Enabled

property/Tool/Grip.description:
Stores the tool's "grip" properties as one `Datatype.CFrame`.

The `Grip` property stores the tool's "grip" properties as a single
`Datatype.CFrame`. These properties position how the player holds the tool
and include `Class.Tool.GripUp|GripUp`, `Class.Tool.GripRight|GripRight`,
`Class.Tool.GripForward|GripForward`, and `Class.Tool.GripPos|GripPos`.
property/Tool/Grip.title: Grip

property/Tool/GripForward.description:
Represents the `R02`, `R12`, and `R22` values of the grip
`Datatype.CFrame` rotation matrix.

One of the properties that specifies a tool's orientation in a character's
hand. This represents the `R02`, `R12`, and `R22` values of the grip
`Datatype.CFrame` rotation matrix.

Other tool properties that control how a character holds a tool include
`Class.Tool.GripUp`, `Class.Tool.GripRight`, and `Class.Tool.GripPos`. All
of these properties are stored in a single `Datatype.CFrame` in the
`Class.Tool.Grip` property.
property/Tool/GripForward.title: GripForward

property/Tool/GripPos.description:
The positional offset of the tool's weld matrix.

This property controls the positional offset of the tool's weld matrix. It
is one of several properties used to position how the player character
holds the tool.

Other properties that control how a character holds a tool include
`Class.Tool.GripUp`, `Class.Tool.GripRight`, and `Class.Tool.GripForward`.
All of these properties are stored in a single `Datatype.CFrame` in the
`Class.Tool.Grip` property.
property/Tool/GripPos.title: GripPos

property/Tool/GripRight.description:
Represents the `R00`, `R10`, and `R20` values of the grip
`Datatype.CFrame` rotation matrix.

One of the properties that specifies a tool's orientation in a character's
hand. This represents the `R00`, `R10`, and `R20` values of the grip
`Datatype.CFrame` rotation matrix.

Other tool properties that control how a character holds a tool include
`Class.Tool.GripUp`, `Class.Tool.GripForward`, and `Class.Tool.GripPos`.
All of these properties are stored in a single `Datatype.CFrame` in the
`Class.Tool.Grip` property.
property/Tool/GripRight.title: GripRight

property/Tool/GripUp.description:
Represents the `R01`, `R11`, and `R21` values of the grip
`Datatype.CFrame` rotation matrix.

One of the properties that specifies a tool's orientation in a character's
hand. This represents the `R01`, `R11`, and `R21` values of the grip
`Datatype.CFrame` rotation matrix.

Other tool properties that control how a character holds a tool include
`Class.Tool.GripRight`, `Class.Tool.GripForward`, and
`Class.Tool.GripPos`. All of these properties are stored in a single
`Datatype.CFrame` in the `Class.Tool.Grip` property.
property/Tool/GripUp.title: GripUp

property/Tool/ManualActivationOnly.description:
Controls whether the `Class.Tool` can be activated without executing
`Class.Tool:Activate()`.

This property controls whether the `Class.Tool` can be activated without
explicitly executing `Class.Tool:Activate()` in a script.

When set to `true`, the tool will only fire `Class.Tool.Activated` when
`Class.Tool:Activate()` is called. This also suppresses the
`Class.ContextActionService:BindActivate()` function.

When set to `false`, mouse clicks (when the tool is equipped) will also
fire `Class.Tool.Activated`.
property/Tool/ManualActivationOnly.title: ManualActivationOnly

property/Tool/RequiresHandle.description:
Determines whether a `Class.Tool` functions without a handle.

This property determines whether a `Class.Tool` functions without a
handle.

A tool has a handle when it contains a child part named **Handle**. Tools
with handles typically require the player equipping them to hold an object
to use them, for instance weapons. Tools without handles typically don't
require the player equipping them to hold anything to use them, for
instance "fly" or "summon" tools.

When set to `true`, the tool will function only with a handle. When set to
`false`, the tool will function even without a handle.
property/Tool/RequiresHandle.title: RequiresHandle

property/Tool/ToolTip.description:
Controls the message displayed when the player's mouse hovers over the
tool in their backpack.

The ToolTip property controls the message that will be displayed when the
player's `Class.Mouse` hovers over the `Class.Tool` in their
`Class.Backpack`.

Generally, the value of this property should describe the what the tool is
or its use. For instance, for a shovel tool, you may choose to set the
ToolTip to:

```lua
tool.ToolTip = "Shovel"
```

or

```lua
tool.ToolTip = "Use to dig"
```

or

```lua
tool.ToolTip = "Shovel - Use to dig"
```
property/Tool/ToolTip.title: ToolTip

property/Torque/RelativeTo.description: The `Datatype.CFrame` in which the torque is expressed.
property/Torque/RelativeTo.title: RelativeTo

property/Torque/Torque.description: The strength and direction of the torque.
property/Torque/Torque.title: Torque

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Coils.description:
The number of coils visualized for the constraint.

This property indicates the number of spring coils for visualization.
Default value is 8.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Coils.title: Coils

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Current.description:
The current angle, in degrees, of the limiting cone.

The current angle, in degrees, of the torsion spring's limiting cone. The
limiting cone is formed at the position of the constraint's
`Class.Constraint.Attachment0|Attachment0` around its secondary axis with
an angle equal to `Class.TorsionSpringConstraint.MaxAngle|MaxAngle`.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Current.title: CurrentAngle

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Damping.description:
Damping constant for the `Class.TorsionSpringConstraint`. Multiplied to
the velocity of the constraint's `Class.Attachment|Attachments` to reduce
the spring force applied.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Damping.title: Damping

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/LimitEn.deprecationMessage:
This property is deprecated. Use
`Class.TorsionSpringConstraint.LimitsEnabled|LimitsEnabled` instead.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/LimitEn.title: LimitEnabled
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/LimitEn.x-roblox-deprecation-message:
This property is deprecated. Use
`Class.TorsionSpringConstraint.LimitsEnabled|LimitsEnabled` instead.

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/LimitsE.description:
Limits the relative angular motion of the secondary axes of attachments
through a cone constraint.

This property, when enabled, limits the relative angular motion of the
secondary axes of attachments through a cone constraint. The default value
is false.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/LimitsE.title: LimitsEnabled

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/MaxAngl.description:
The maximum angle of the constraint's limiting cone.

This property determines the maximum angle (in degrees) of the torsion
spring's limiting cone. The limiting cone is formed at the position of the
constraint's `Class.Constraint.Attachment0|Attachment0` around its
secondary axis with an angle equal to
`Class.TorsionSpringConstraint.MaxAngle|MaxAngle`. Default value is 45
degrees.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/MaxAngl.title: MaxAngle

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/MaxTorq.description:
The maximum allowable torque provided by the torsion spring.

This property determines the maximum torque supported by the torsion
spring. Defaults to 1000.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/MaxTorq.title: MaxTorque

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Radius.description:
The visualization radius of the spring.

This property indicates the visualization radius of the spring, in studs.
Default value is 0.4.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Radius.title: Radius

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Restitu.description:
The restitution coefficient of the cone constraint.

This property defines how elastic `Class.Attachment|Attachments` connected
by a `Class.TorsionSpringConstraint` are when they reach the end of the
range specified by `Class.TorsionSpringConstraint.MaxAngle|MaxAngle`, when
`Class.TorsionSpringConstraint.LimitEnabled|LimitEnabled` is true. The
value defaults to 0 and can be any floating number within the range of 0
and 1.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Restitu.title: Restitution

property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Stiffne.description:
The torsional stiffness of the spring.

In the absence of damping, this property is proportional to the opposing
torque of the spring. For instance, higher stiffness results in a larger
opposing torque, and smaller stiffness results in a smaller opposing
torque. The larger the torque value, the faster the axes are pushed
together when the relative angle is positive (or away from each other if
the relative angle is negative). The value defaults to 100.
property/TorsionSpringConstraint/Stiffne.title: Stiffness

property/Trail/Attachment0.description:
Along with `Class.Trail.Attachment1|Attachment1`, determines where the
trail will start drawing its segments.

A `Class.Trail` starts drawing its segments at the positions of its
**Attachment0** and `Class.Trail.Attachment1|Attachment1`. When the trail
is `Class.Trail.Enabled|Enabled`, it records the positions of its
attachments every frame and connects these positions to the attachments'
positions on the previous frame, creating a polygon that is then filled in
by the trail's `Class.Trail.Color|Color` and
`Class.Trail.Texture|Texture`.

Changing the attachments of a trail while a trail is drawing will remove
all of the segments the trail has already drawn.
property/Trail/Attachment0.title: Attachment0

property/Trail/Attachment1.description:
Along with `Class.Trail.Attachment0|Attachment0`, determines where the
trail will start drawing its segments.

A `Class.Trail` starts drawing its segments at the positions of its
`Class.Trail.Attachment0|Attachment0` and **Attachment1**. When the trail
is `Class.Trail.Enabled|Enabled`, it records the positions of its
attachments every frame and connects these positions to the attachments'
positions on the previous frame, creating a polygon that is then filled in
by the trail's `Class.Trail.Color|Color` and
`Class.Trail.Texture|Texture`.

Changing the attachments of a trail while a trail is drawing will remove
all of the segments the trail has already drawn.
property/Trail/Attachment1.title: Attachment1

property/Trail/Brightness.description:
Scales the light emitted from the trail when
`Class.Trail.LightInfluence|LightInfluence` is less than 1.

Scales the light emitted from the trail when
`Class.Trail.LightInfluence|LightInfluence` is less than 1. This property
is 1 by default and can set to any number within the range of 0 to 10000.
Increasing the value of `Class.Trail.LightInfluence|LightInfluence`
decreases the effect of this property's value.
property/Trail/Brightness.title: Brightness

property/Trail/Color.description:
The color of the trail throughout its lifetime.

Determines the color of the trail throughout its lifetime. If
`Class.Trail.Texture|Texture` is set, this color will tint the texture.

This property is a `Datatype.ColorSequence`, allowing the color to be
configured to vary across the length of the trail. If the color changes
after some of the trail segments have been drawn, all of the old segments
will be updated to match the new colors.
property/Trail/Color.title: Color

property/Trail/Enabled.description:
Determines whether the trail will be drawn or not.

This property determines whether the trail will be drawn or not.

If set to `false` while a trail is drawing, no new segments will be drawn,
but any existing segments will be cleaned up naturally when they reach the
end of their `Class.Trail.Lifetime|Lifetime`. To forcibly clean up
existing segments, call the `Class.Trail:Clear()|Clear()` method at the
same time.
property/Trail/Enabled.title: Enabled

property/Trail/FaceCamera.description:
Determines whether the trail will always face the camera, regardless of
its orientation.

A `Class.Trail` is a 2D projection existing in 3D space, meaning that it
may not be visible from every angle. The **FaceCamera** property, when set
to `true`, ensures that the trail always faces the
`Class.Workspace.CurrentCamera|CurrentCamera`, regardless of its
orientation.

Changing this property immediately affects all existing and future trail
segments.
property/Trail/FaceCamera.title: FaceCamera

property/Trail/Lifetime.description:
