property/UserInputService/PreferredInput.description:
Queries the primary input type a player is using, based on anticipated user behavior. This read-only property lets you query the **primary** input type a player is likely using, based on anticipated user behavior, to ensure UI elements like on‑screen buttons and menus work elegantly across devices. For example, a touch‑enabled device assumes touch is the default input and that touch buttons may appear for actions, but if a player connects an additional bluetooth keyboard/mouse or gamepad, you can assume they want to switch to that as the primary input type and possibly use touch as a backup input for on‑screen UI. The value of `PreferredInput` changes based on built‑in device inputs and the player's most recent interaction with a connected gamepad or keyboard/mouse. Examples include:
Real-World Scenario PreferredInput
Player is using a phone with no other connected input devices; no possibility of an input type change. Enum.PreferredInput|Touch
Player is using a mobile device with a bluetooth keyboard & mouse connected, but no gamepad is connected. Enum.PreferredInput|KeyboardAndMouse
Player is using a tablet with a bluetooth gamepad connected, but no keyboard or mouse is connected. Enum.PreferredInput|Gamepad
Player is using an Xbox or PlayStation with a bluetooth keyboard & mouse connected and has most recently interacted with the keyboard or mouse. Enum.PreferredInput|KeyboardAndMouse
Player is on a Windows or Mac PC with a gamepad connected and has most recently interacted with the gamepad. Enum.PreferredInput|Gamepad
property/UserInputService/PreferredInput.title: PreferredInput

property/UserInputService/TouchEnabled.description:
Describes whether the user's device has a touch screen available.

This property describes whether the user's device has a touch screen
available. If `true`, you can use touch‑related events such as
`Class.UserInputService.TouchStarted|TouchStarted` and
`Class.UserInputService.TouchMoved|TouchMoved`.

For seamless cross-platform compatibility on mixed-input devices, see
`Class.UserInputService.PreferredInput|PreferredInput` which more
accurately reflects which input (mouse/keyboard, touch, gamepad, etc.) the
player is likely using as the **primary** input.
property/UserInputService/TouchEnabled.title: TouchEnabled

property/UserInputService/TouchScreenEna.description:
Describes whether the user's device has a touch screen, reflecting the
device's true hardware capability.

Read-only. Whether the user's device has a touch screen. Defaults to
`false`; the engine sets it to `true` on devices with a physical touch
screen.

Unlike `Class.UserInputService.TouchEnabled|TouchEnabled`, which reports
`false` on some touch-capable desktop hardware (such as a Windows laptop
with a touch screen) to avoid switching those devices to mobile-style
controls, `TouchScreenEnabled` reflects the device's true touch
capability.
property/UserInputService/TouchScreenEna.title: TouchScreenEnabled

property/VRService/AutomaticScaling.description:
Automatically adjusts scaling in VR to align the player with their avatar.

property/VRService/AvatarGestures.description:

their controllers and headset.

using their controllers and headset. Set this to `false` for experiences
where VR hand and head tracking conflicts with custom game mechanics, such

This property must be set on the server.

property/VRService/ControllerModels.description:

the experience.

Controls how the models representing the player's VR hand controllers are
displayed (`Enum.VRControllerModelMode`). When set to
`Enum.VRControllerModelMode.Transparent|Transparent`, the controller

not rendered.

property/VRService/ControllerModels.title: ControllerModels

property/VRService/FadeOutViewOnCollisio.description:

When true, a VR player's view fades to black when their head collides with
an object. This property prevents players from being able to see through
walls while in VR. The default value is true.

property/VRService/GuiInputUserCFrame.description:

property will be `Enum.UserCFrame.Head`.

property.
property/VRService/GuiInputUserCFrame.title: GuiInputUserCFrame

property/VRService/LaserPointer.description:

user interface is displayed.

Controls the mode of the laser pointer that a VR player uses to point at
and interact with the user interface (`Enum.VRLaserPointerMode`). Set it
to `Enum.VRLaserPointerMode.Disabled|Disabled` to hide the laser pointer,
`Enum.VRLaserPointerMode.Pointer|Pointer` to show a single pointer, or
`Enum.VRLaserPointerMode.DualPointer|DualPointer` to show a pointer for

Defaults to `Enum.VRLaserPointerMode.Pointer|Pointer`.
property/VRService/LaserPointer.title: LaserPointer

property/VRService/ThirdPersonFollowCamE.description:

user.

Read-only. Indicates whether the third-person follow camera is enabled for
the VR user. Its value mirrors the user's VR comfort setting and updates
automatically whenever the user changes that setting, firing a changed
signal so that scripts can respond. It cannot be set from a script.
property/VRService/ThirdPersonFollowCamE.title: ThirdPersonFollowCamEnabled

property/VRService/VREnabled.description:
Describes whether the user is using a virtual reality device.

This property describes whether the user is using a virtual reality (VR)
device.

If a VR device is enabled, you can interact with its location and movement
through methods such as `Class.UserInputService:GetUserCFrame()`. You can
also react to VR device movement using the
`Class.UserInputService.UserCFrameChanged` event.

```lua
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local isUsingVR = UserInputService.VREnabled
if isUsingVR then
	print("User is using a VR headset!")
else
	print("User is not using a VR headset!")
end
```

This property can only be used in a `Class.LocalScript`.

#### See Also

- `Class.Camera.HeadLocked`
- `Class.UserInputService:GetUserCFrame()`
- `Class.UserInputService.UserCFrameChanged`

property/VideoDisplay/ResampleMode.description:
Selects the texture resampling mode for the `Class.VideoDisplay`.

Determines how the video looks when it is scaled. By default, the video
smooths out texturing when displayed on the screen larger or smaller than
its size in texture memory. When set to
`Enum.ResamplerMode.Pixelated|Enum.ResamplerMode.Pixelated`, the video
preserves the sharp edges of pixels.
property/VideoDisplay/ResampleMode.title: ResampleMode

property/VideoDisplay/ScaleType.description:
Determines how a video will scale if displayed in a UI element whose
aspect ratio differs from the source video.

Determines how a video texture is rendered when the UI element's aspect
ratio differs from the source video's aspect ratio.

By default, this property is `Enum.ScaleType.Stretch` which will simply
stretch/compact the video texture dimensions so it fits the UI element's
space exactly.
property/VideoDisplay/ScaleType.title: ScaleType

property/VideoDisplay/TileSize.description:
Sets the tiling size of the `Class.VideoDisplay`.

default of
<Typography noWrap>`Datatype.UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)`</Typography>. Tiling
starts at the top-left corner of the video. This property is only active

`Class.VideoDisplay` is set to `Enum.ScaleType.Tile`.

property/VideoDisplay/VideoColor3.description:

property/VideoDisplay/VideoRectOffset.description:

dimension is set to `0`, the entire video is displayed instead.

property/VideoDisplay/VideoTransparency.description:

property/VideoFrame/RollOffMaxDistance.description:
The maximum distance, in studs, a listener can be from the video's part
and still hear its audio.

The maximum distance, in studs, a client's listener can be from the
`Class.VideoFrame`'s part and still hear its audio. Defaults to `10000`.

This property only affects playback when the `Class.VideoFrame` is 3D, as
described in the class's "2D and 3D Sound" section; it has no effect on a

property/VideoFrame/RollOffMinDistance.description:

attenuate.

begins to attenuate (decrease in volume). Defaults to `1`.

described in the class's "2D and 3D Sound" section; it has no effect on a
global `Class.VideoFrame`. How `RollOffMinDistance` affects the
attenuation of the sound depends on the
`Class.VideoFrame.RollOffMode|RollOffMode` property.

property/VideoFrame/Video.description:

with.

with. To save resources and improve performance, set this property to `""`
when the `Class.VideoFrame` is not visible or in use.

property/VideoFrame/VideoContent.description:
The video content a `Class.VideoFrame` is associated with, as either an
asset content ID (same value as `Class.VideoFrame.Video|Video`) or a
direct reference to a `Class.VideoCapture` object for local screen
recordings.

The video content a `Class.VideoFrame` object is associated with. Setting
this property is equivalent to setting `Class.VideoFrame.Video|Video`, and
reading it returns a content ID equal to `Class.VideoFrame.Video|Video`.

When referencing a video by content ID, build the value with the
corresponding `Datatype.Content` constructor:
`Datatype.Content.fromAssetId()` for a numeric asset ID, or
`Datatype.Content.fromUri()` for an `rbxassetid://` URI.

Unlike `Class.VideoFrame.Video|Video`, which only accepts a content ID
string, `VideoContent` can also hold a direct reference to a
`Class.VideoCapture` object, such as one retrieved through
`Class.CaptureService:ReadCapturesFromGalleryAsync()`. This lets a local
screen recording play back on the `VideoFrame` without first uploading it
to Roblox. Build the value with `Datatype.Content.fromObject()`, for
example `videoFrame.VideoContent = Content.fromObject(capture)`.

Indicates the length of the `Class.VideoPlayer.VideoContent|VideoContent`
in seconds.

This property indicates the length of the
`Class.VideoPlayer.VideoContent|VideoContent` in seconds. If the video is
not loaded, this value is 0.
property/VideoPlayer/TimeLength.title: TimeLength

property/VideoPlayer/TimePosition.description:
Indicates the progress in seconds of the
`Class.VideoPlayer.VideoContent|VideoContent`.

This property indicates the progress in seconds of the
`Class.VideoPlayer.VideoContent|VideoContent`. It can be changed to move
the playback position of the video both before and during playback.
property/VideoPlayer/TimePosition.title: TimePosition

property/VideoPlayer/VideoContent.description:
The asset to be loaded into the `Class.VideoPlayer`.

The content ID of the video file a `Class.VideoPlayer` object is
associated with. To save resources and improve performance, call the
`Class.VideoPlayer:Unload()|Unload()` method to unload the
`Class.VideoPlayer.VideoContent|VideoContent` when the `Class.VideoPlayer`
is not visible or in use.
property/VideoPlayer/VideoContent.title: VideoContent

property/VideoPlayer/Volume.description:
Controls how loudly the audio track will be played.

Volume level, which is multiplied onto the output audio stream,
controlling how loudly the audio track plays. Ranges from 0 to 3.
property/VideoPlayer/Volume.title: Volume

property/VideoSampler/TimeLength.description:
The length of the `Class.VideoSampler.VideoContent|VideoContent` in
seconds.
property/VideoSampler/TimeLength.title: TimeLength

property/ViewportFrame/Ambient.description:
The lighting hue applied to the area within the `ViewportFrame`.

This property determines the lighting hue applied to the area within the
`ViewportFrame`. Defaults to
<Typography noWrap>`Datatype.Color3|Color3.fromRGB(200, 200, 200)`</Typography>
(ghost grey).
property/ViewportFrame/Ambient.title: Ambient

property/ViewportFrame/CurrentCamera.description:
`Class.Camera` that is used to render children objects.

`Class.Camera` instance that is used to render children objects. Defaults
to `nil`.

The `Class.Camera` object does not replicate so the
`Class.ViewportFrame.CurrentCamera` won't replicate either. When you set
this property, `Class.Camera.CFrame` and `Class.Camera.FieldOfView` will
be saved and replicate with the `ViewportFrame` internally so the client
can render the frame without a `Class.Camera` object.
property/ViewportFrame/CurrentCamera.title: CurrentCamera

property/ViewportFrame/ImageColor3.description:
Determines how the rendered viewport image will be colorized.

This property determines how the rendered viewport image will be
colorized, allowing you to change the color without directly modifying the
rendered object. The default colorization value is <Typography
noWrap>`Datatype.Color3|Color3.new(1, 1, 1)`</Typography> (white) at which
no color modification occurs.

See also `Class.ViewportFrame.ImageTransparency|ImageTransparency` which
determines the transparency of the rendered image.
property/ViewportFrame/ImageColor3.title: ImageColor3

property/ViewportFrame/ImageTransparency.description:
Determines the transparency of the rendered viewport image.

This property determines the transparency of the rendered viewport image,
allowing you to change the transparency without directly modifying the
rendered object. A value of `0` (default) is completely opaque and a value
of `1` is completely transparent (invisible).

See also `Class.ViewportFrame.ImageColor3|ImageColor3` which determines
how the rendered image will be colorized.
property/ViewportFrame/ImageTransparency.title: ImageTransparency

property/ViewportFrame/LightColor.description:
The color of the emitted light.

The color of the emitted light. Defaults to
<Typography noWrap>`Datatype.Color3|Color3.fromRGB(140, 140, 140)`</Typography>
(silver).
property/ViewportFrame/LightColor.title: LightColor

property/ViewportFrame/LightDirection.description:
A `Datatype.Vector3` representing the direction of the light source.

A `Datatype.Vector3` representing the direction of the light source from
position <Typography noWrap>`(0, 0, 0)`</Typography>. Defaults to
<Typography noWrap>`Datatype.Vector3|Vector3.new(-1, -1, -1)`</Typography>.
property/ViewportFrame/LightDirection.title: LightDirection

property/VoiceChatService/DefaultDistanc.description:
Determines which distance attenuation curve the default voice chat setup
uses when `Class.AudioDeviceInput` and `Class.AudioEmitter` objects are
generated.

This property controls the default distance attenuation curve assigned to
any generated `Class.AudioEmitter` instances in the default voice chat
setup.

This property only has an effect if
`Class.VoiceChatService.EnableDefaultVoice|EnableDefaultVoice` and
`Class.VoiceChatService.UseAudioApi|UseAudioApi` are both enabled, since
no `Class.AudioEmitter|AudioEmitters` are otherwise generated.
property/VoiceChatService/DefaultDistanc.title: DefaultDistanceAttenuation

property/VoiceChatService/EnableDefaultV.description:
Controls whether each voice-eligible player can be heard as though they
were speaking through their character.

When enabled, each voice-eligible player can be heard as though they were
speaking through their character. The implementation details of the voice
setup depend on `Class.VoiceChatService.UseAudioApi|UseAudioApi`.

When `Class.VoiceChatService.UseAudioApi|UseAudioApi` is
`Enum.AudioApiRollout|Enabled`, disabling this property disables the
default setup, but `Class.AudioDeviceInput` will still work. Conversely,
when `Class.VoiceChatService.UseAudioApi|UseAudioApi` is
`Enum.AudioApiRollout|Disabled`, disabling the default voice setup
effectively disables voice chat altogether.
property/VoiceChatService/EnableDefaultV.title: EnableDefaultVoice

property/VoiceChatService/UseAudioApi.description:
Controls whether voice chat is represented and controlled by
`Class.AudioDeviceInput` objects.

If `Enum.AudioApiRollout|Enabled`, the voice chat setup is represented and
controlled by `Class.AudioDeviceInput` objects. More specifically:

- An `Class.AudioDeviceInput` will be created and parented to each
  voice-eligible `Class.Player`.
- An `Class.AudioEmitter` will be created and parented to each
  voice-eligible player's `Class.Player.Character`.
- An `Class.AudioListener` will be created and parented to
  `Class.Workspace.CurrentCamera`.

You can disable the default setup by setting
`Class.VoiceChatService.EnableDefaultVoice` to `false`.

If `Enum.AudioApiRollout|Disabled`, the voice chat setup is done through
an internal-only system.

Currently, setting this to `Enum.AudioApiRollout|Automatic` has the same
meaning as `Enum.AudioApiRollout|Disabled`. However, in the future,
`Enum.AudioApiRollout|Automatic` will become
`Enum.AudioApiRollout|Enabled`, so that new experiences can achieve
greater customization over voice.
property/VoiceChatService/UseAudioApi.title: UseAudioApi

property/WeldConstraint/Active.description:
Indicates if the WeldConstraint is currently active in the world.

True if the WeldConstraint is currently active in the world.

If the WeldConstraint or one of its parts is not in `Class.Workspace` the
weld will be inactive.

Rigid joints like `Class.Weld`, `Class.Snap`, `Class.WeldConstraint`,
`Class.Motor`, or `Class.Motor6D` may also be disabled due to conflicts
with other rigid joints, such as joints between the same two parts or
indirect cycles in the weld graph. Joints disabled this way may be
re-enabled later when another joint or part is added or removed.

Duplicate WeldConstraints do not conflict because WeldConstraints derive
their internal CFrames from the relative positions of their parts when
they are enabled and all update when `Class.BasePart.Position` or
`Class.BasePart.Orientation` is set on a part. The spanning tree may still
disable them if they are redundant or form a cycle.
property/WeldConstraint/Active.title: Active

property/WeldConstraint/Enabled.description:
Toggles the constraint on and off.

The **Enabled** property of a `Class.WeldConstraint` sets whether the
constraint is active or not. When this property is set to true, if the
constraint's `Class.WeldConstraint.Part0` and `Class.WeldConstraint.Part1`
properties are set, then the constraint will ensure that its two connected
parts will be locked together.
property/WeldConstraint/Enabled.title: Enabled

property/WeldConstraint/Part0.description:
The first part connected by the constraint.

The `Part0` and `Class.WeldConstraint.Part1` properties of a
`Class.WeldConstraint` set which two `Class.BasePart` the weld connects.
As soon as both properties are set and the weld is
`Class.WeldConstraint.Enabled`, the weld will lock the two parts together.

If `Part0` or `Part1` are ever set to new parts, then the `WeldConstraint`
will instantly link the new part. The old part will no longer be
constrained.
property/WeldConstraint/Part0.title: Part0

property/WeldConstraint/Part1.description:
The second part connected by the constraint.

The `Class.WeldConstraint.Part0` and `Part1` properties of a
`Class.WeldConstraint` set which two `Class.BasePart` the weld connects.
As soon as both properties are set and the weld is
`Class.WeldConstraint.Enabled`, the weld will lock the two parts together.

If `Part0` or `Part1` are ever set to new parts, then the `WeldConstraint`
will instantly link the new part. The old part will no longer be
constrained.
property/WeldConstraint/Part1.title: Part1

property/Wire/Connected.description:
Denotes whether the `Class.Wire` is carrying a stream of data.

Denotes whether the `Class.Wire` is connected, meaning its
`Class.Wire.SourceInstance|SourceInstance`,
`Class.Wire.TargetInstance|TargetInstance`,
`Class.Wire.SourceName|SourceName`, and `Class.Wire.TargetName|TargetName`
properties are all assigned, the corresponding
`Class.Wire.SourceName|SourceName` and `Class.Wire.TargetName|TargetName`
pins exist on `Class.Wire.SourceInstance|SourceInstance` and
`Class.Wire.TargetInstance|TargetInstance` respectively, and the
connection does not result in a cyclic processing graph.
property/Wire/Connected.title: Connected

property/Wire/SourceInstance.description:
The `Class.Instance` producing a stream to be carried over the wire.

The `Class.Instance` producing a stream to be carried over the wire. At
the moment, only audio streams are wirable.
property/Wire/SourceInstance.title: SourceInstance

property/Wire/SourceName.description:
The name of the pin on `Class.Wire.SourceInstance|SourceInstance` that is
producing a stream.

The name of the pin on `Class.Wire.SourceInstance|SourceInstance` that is
producing a stream. At the moment, various audio instances only have an
**Output** pin, but this may expand in the future. The default value of
this property is **Output** so it is not yet necessary to change.
property/Wire/SourceName.title: SourceName

property/Wire/TargetInstance.description:
The `Class.Instance` to receive a stream from
`Class.Wire.SourceInstance|SourceInstance`.

The `Class.Instance` intended to receive a stream from
`Class.Wire.SourceInstance|SourceInstance`. Currently, only audio streams
are wirable.
property/Wire/TargetInstance.title: TargetInstance

property/Wire/TargetName.description:
The name of the pin on `Class.Wire.TargetInstance|TargetInstance` that is
receiving a stream.

The name of the pin on `Class.Wire.TargetInstance|TargetInstance` that is
receiving a stream. At the moment, audio instances typically have an
**Input** pin, but `Class.AudioCompressor` has an additional **Sidechain**
pin. This may expand in the future.
property/Wire/TargetName.title: TargetName

property/WireframeHandleAdornment/Scale.description:
The **XYZ** scale of the wireframe adornment.

This property specifies the **XYZ** scale of the wireframe adornment as a
`Datatype.Vector3`. For example, a scale of
`Datatype.Vector3.new(1, 2, 1)` will scale the adornment twice its normal
size on the **Y** axis while keeping the **X** and **Z** axes unchanged.
property/WireframeHandleAdornment/Scale.title: Scale

property/WireframeHandleAdornment/Thickn.description:
Thickness of the wireframe adornment's lines in pixels.

This property determines the thickness of the wireframe adornment's lines
in pixels. Note that this visual thickness does not change relative to the
adornment's distance from the viewer's camera.
property/WireframeHandleAdornment/Thickn.title: Thickness

property/Workspace/AirDensity.description:
The air density at ground level, used in the aerodynamic force model.

The ground level (**Y** of 0) air density in RMU/stud³ units (see
[Roblox Units](../../../physics/units.md)), used to calculate the
aerodynamic force if `Class.Workspace.FluidForces` is
`Enum.FluidForces|Experimental`. The default corresponds to realistic sea
level air density at standard temperature and pressure. Air density decays
as the **Y** altitude increases, reaching 5% of its ground level value at
100,000 studs. Below **Y** of 0, the air density is fixed at the input
value.
property/Workspace/AirDensity.title: AirDensity

property/Workspace/AirTurbulenceIntensit.description:
Controls the strength of turbulence present in the wind velocity field,
affecting the aerodynamic force model.

Controls the intensity of turbulence by determining the magnitude of
fluctuations in wind velocities. Ranges from `0` to `1`, with a value of
`0` disabling turbulence and a value of `1` providing the most intense
turbulence. The values of `AirTurbulenceIntensity` roughly correspond to
the following levels:

- `(0, 0.4]`: Low intensity turbulence
- `(0.4, 0.7]`: Moderate intensity turbulence
- `(0.7, 1]`: High intensity turbulence

The magnitude of the fluctuations at a fixed intensity scale linearly with
the magnitude of the global wind, except in the case that the global wind
is zero. When the global wind is zero, the magnitude of the fluctuations
scale exponentially with `AirTurbulenceIntensity`, allowing low and high
intensity turbulence to exist with wind velocities that still average out
to zero.
property/Workspace/AirTurbulenceIntensit.title: AirTurbulenceIntensity

property/Workspace/AllowThirdPartySales.description:
Determines whether assets created by other users can be sold in the game.

This `Class.Workspace` property determines whether assets created by other
uses can be sold in the game.
property/Workspace/AllowThirdPartySales.title: AllowThirdPartySales

property/Workspace/AuthorityMode.description:
Sets the server authority mode.

Sets the server authority mode. See `Enum.AuthorityMode` for options.
property/Workspace/AuthorityMode.title: AuthorityMode

property/Workspace/AvatarUnificationMode.description:
Enables the R6 to R15 adapter, allowing R15 avatars to join R6
experiences.

When `Enum.AvatarUnificationMode.Enabled`, R15 avatars can join R6
experiences via the R6 to R15 adapter. R15 characters receive invisible
adapter parts with R6-compatible names welded to their corresponding R15
parts, preserving R6-like scale and movement while enabling R15 features
such as layered clothing and animatable heads. Only relevant when the
experience's avatar type is set to R6.
property/Workspace/AvatarUnificationMode.title: AvatarUnificationMode

property/Workspace/ClientAnimatorThrottl.description:
Specifies the animation throttling mode for the local client.

Specifies the `Enum.ClientAnimatorThrottlingMode` to use for the local
client.

When enabled, animations on remotely-simulated `Class.Model` instances
will begin to throttle. The throttler calculates throttling intensity
using:

- Visibility of a `Class.Model` in relation to the `Class.Camera`
- In-game FPS
- Number of active animations
property/Workspace/ClientAnimatorThrottl.title: ClientAnimatorThrottling

property/Workspace/CurrentCamera.description:
The `Class.Camera` object being used by the local player.

The `Class.Camera` object being used by the local player.

#### How to use CurrentCamera

When looking for a client's `Class.Camera` object, use this property
rather than looking for a child of `Class.Workspace` named "Camera".

When you set this property, all other `Camera` objects in the `Workspace`
are destroyed, including the previous `CurrentCamera`. If you set this
property to `nil` or to a camera that is not a descendant of the Workspace
(or the `CurrentCamera` is otherwise destroyed), a new `Camera` will be
created and assigned. Avoid these scenarios, as destroying the camera can
have unintended consequences.

For more information, see
[Scripting the Camera](../../../workspace/camera.md#scripting-the-camera).
property/Workspace/CurrentCamera.title: CurrentCamera

property/Workspace/DistributedGameTime.description:
The amount of time, in seconds, that the game has been running.

The amount of time, in seconds, that the game has been running.

Despite the title, this value is currently not 'Distributed' across the
client and the server. Instead, on the server it represents how long the
server has been running. On the client, it represents how long the client
has been connected to the server.

Developers should not rely on the above behavior, and it is possible this
property will be synchronized across clients and the server in the future.

Those looking for the time since the program started running should use
the 'time' function instead. See below for a comparison between
DistributedGameTime and its alternatives.
property/Workspace/DistributedGameTime.title: DistributedGameTime

property/Workspace/EnableSLIMAvatars.description:
Controls whether SLIM rendering is used for avatars in the experience.

This `Enum.RolloutState` property controls whether a
`Enum.ModelLevelOfDetail|SLIM` model is generated for avatar characters in
the experience. When enabled and instance streaming is active, avatars
render using SLIM in the same way that setting `Class.Model.LevelOfDetail`
to `Enum.ModelLevelOfDetail|SLIM` works for other models.

When set to `Enum.RolloutState|Enabled`, avatars use SLIM rendering. When
set to `Enum.RolloutState|Disabled`, avatars use the traditional rendering
approach. `Enum.RolloutState|Default` follows the current engine-wide
rollout state.

This property cannot be set through developer-facing Luau and must be set
in Studio through the Properties window, Command Bar, or a plugin.
property/Workspace/EnableSLIMAvatars.title: EnableSLIMAvatars

property/Workspace/FallHeightEnabled.description:
Controls whether parts that fall below
`Class.Workspace.FallenPartsDestroyHeight` are automatically destroyed.

When `false`, the kill plane defined by
`Class.Workspace.FallenPartsDestroyHeight` is disabled and falling parts
are not automatically removed. Defaults to `true`.

This property can be read by scripts but can only be set by plugins, the
command bar, or the properties window in Studio.
property/Workspace/FallHeightEnabled.title: FallHeightEnabled

property/Workspace/FallenPartsDestroyHei.description:
Determines the height at which falling `Class.BasePart|BaseParts` and
their ancestor `Class.Model|Models` are removed from `Class.Workspace`.

This property determines the height at which the engine automatically
removes falling `Class.BasePart|BaseParts` and their ancestor
`Class.Model|Models` from `Class.Workspace` by parenting them to `nil`.
This is to prevent parts that have fallen off the map from continuing to
fall forever.

If a part removed due to this behavior is the last part in a
`Class.Model`, that model will also be removed. This applies to all model
ancestors of the part.

This property is clamped between -50,000 and 50,000 because
`Class.BasePart|BaseParts` do not simulate or render properly at a great
distance from the origin due to floating point inaccuracies.

This property can be read by scripts, but can only be set by plugins, the
command bar, or the properties window in Studio.
property/Workspace/FallenPartsDestroyHei.title: FallenPartsDestroyHeight

property/Workspace/FilteringEnabled.description:
Determines whether changes made from the client will replicate to the
server or not.

This property is discontinued and no longer takes effect.
property/Workspace/FilteringEnabled.title: FilteringEnabled

property/Workspace/FluidForces.description:
Determines whether the physics engine computes aerodynamic forces on
`Class.BasePart|BaseParts` whose
`Class.BasePart.EnableFluidForces|EnableFluidForces` property is true.

With this property enabled, the physics engine computes aerodynamic forces
on `Class.BasePart|BaseParts` whose
`Class.BasePart.EnableFluidForces|EnableFluidForces` property is true. The
default, `Enum.FluidForces|Default`, disables aerodynamic forces. Note
that this property cannot be set through developer-facing Luau and instead
must be toggled in Studio.
property/Workspace/FluidForces.title: FluidForces

property/Workspace/GlobalWind.description:
Specifies the global wind vector for animated terrain grass, dynamic
clouds, and particles.

This property specifies the direction and strength that wind blows through
the experience, affecting terrain grass, dynamic clouds, and particles.
See the [Global Wind](../../../environment/global-wind.md) article for
details.
property/Workspace/GlobalWind.title: GlobalWind

property/Workspace/Gravity.description:
Determines the acceleration due to gravity applied to falling
`Class.BasePart|BaseParts`.

Determines the acceleration due to gravity applied to falling
`Class.BasePart|BaseParts`. This value is measured in studs per second
squared and by default is set to 196.2 studs/second<sup>2</sup>. By
changing this value, developers can simulate the effects of lower or
higher gravity in game.
property/Workspace/Gravity.title: Gravity

property/Workspace/IKControlConstraintSu.description:
Enables support for constraints for IKControls. If disabled, IKControls
ignore physics constraints.

Enables support for constraints for IKControls. The `Default` value is the
same as `Enabled`. If disabled, IKControls ignore physics constraints. See
`Class.IKControl` for additional details.
property/Workspace/IKControlConstraintSu.title: IKControlConstraintSupport

property/Workspace/ImprovedAnimationCons.description:
Controls whether `Class.AnimationConstraint|AnimationConstraints` use the
improved soft-formulation controller.

Controls whether `Class.AnimationConstraint|AnimationConstraints` drive
their target using an improved soft controller based on strength and
damping instead of the legacy proportional-derivative controller.

`Enum.RolloutState|Default` follows the current engine-wide rollout state.
property/Workspace/ImprovedAnimationCons.title: ImprovedAnimationConstraint

property/Workspace/ImprovedPhysicsReplic.description:
Controls whether the experience uses the improved physics replication path
between the server and clients.

Controls whether physics uses the improved state replication path when
sending physics state between the server and clients. When set to
`Enum.RolloutState|Enabled`, the server advertises this configuration so
connected clients enable the improved path. Setting it to
`Enum.RolloutState|Disabled` opts the place out.

`Enum.RolloutState|Default` follows the current engine-wide rollout state.
property/Workspace/ImprovedPhysicsReplic.title: ImprovedPhysicsReplication

property/Workspace/InsertPoint.description:
The world position at which new objects are placed when inserted from the
toolbox.

Stores the world-space position used when inserting new objects into the
workspace via the Studio IDE.
property/Workspace/InsertPoint.title: InsertPoint

property/Workspace/InterpolationThrottli.deprecationMessage: This property should not be used for new work.
property/Workspace/InterpolationThrottli.title: InterpolationThrottling
property/Workspace/InterpolationThrottli.x-roblox-deprecation-message: This property should not be used for new work.

property/Workspace/LayeredClothingCacheO.description:
Controls whether layered clothing cache optimizations are enabled.

Controls whether the engine caches layered clothing rendering data to
improve performance for experiences with many characters wearing layered
clothing. `Enum.RolloutState|Default` follows the current engine-wide
rollout state.
property/Workspace/LayeredClothingCacheO.title: LayeredClothingCacheOptimizations

property/Workspace/LuauTypeCheckMode.description:
Sets the Luau type checking mode for scripts in the experience.

Controls the Luau type checking mode applied to scripts in the experience.
See `Enum.LuauTypeCheckMode` for the available modes.
property/Workspace/LuauTypeCheckMode.title: LuauTypeCheckMode

property/Workspace/MeshPartHeadsAndAcces.description:
Sets whether character Heads and Accessories should be downloaded as
MeshParts.

Sets whether character Heads and Accessories should be downloaded as
`Class.MeshPart|MeshParts`. The `Default` value is the same as `Enabled`.
If this feature is enabled, built-in avatars will use
`Class.MeshPart|MeshParts` for the character's head and accessories.
property/Workspace/MeshPartHeadsAndAcces.title: MeshPartHeadsAndAccessories

property/Workspace/MeshStreamingAndImpro.description:
Controls whether the experience uses the new mesh streaming and improved
LOD system.

This `Enum.RolloutState` property determines whether the experience uses
the new mesh streaming and Wild Mesh Simplifier LOD system. When set to
`Enum.RolloutState|Enabled`, mesh requests fetch the lowest quality LOD
first and stream in higher detail over time. When set to
`Enum.RolloutState|Disabled`, the legacy mesh loading behavior is used.
`Enum.RolloutState|Default` follows the current engine-wide rollout state.
property/Workspace/MeshStreamingAndImpro.title: MeshStreamingAndImprovedLods

property/Workspace/ModelStreamingBehavio.description:
Controls how `Class.Model|Models` are replicated in experiences when
instance streaming is enabled.

This `Enum.ModelStreamingBehavior` property controls how
`Class.Model|Models` are replicated in experiences when instance streaming
is enabled.
property/Workspace/ModelStreamingBehavio.title: ModelStreamingBehavior

property/Workspace/NextGenerationReplica.description:
When `true`, enables an alternate replication system that alters and
improves how properties are replicated under the hood.

When `true`, enables an alternate replication system that alters and
improves how properties are replicated under the hood; note that when
`true`, you should not rely on the ordering of property replication and
remote events.
property/Workspace/NextGenerationReplica.title: NextGenerationReplication

property/Workspace/PathfindingUseImprove.description:
Controls whether an improved search algorithm is used by
`Class.PathfindingService`.

When `Enum.PathfindingUseImprovedSearch|Enabled`,
`Class.PathfindingService` uses an improved pathfinding algorithm.
`Enum.PathfindingUseImprovedSearch|Default` follows the current
engine-wide rollout state.
property/Workspace/PathfindingUseImprove.title: PathfindingUseImprovedSearch

property/Workspace/PhysicsSteppingMethod.description:
Sets how the solver will advance the physics simulation forward in time.

Sets how the solver will advance the physics simulation forward in time.
This option cannot be set through developer-facing Luau and must be set
from the **PhysicsSteppingMethod** property of **Workspace** within
Studio. See
[Adaptive Timestepping](../../../physics/adaptive-timestepping.md) for
details.

Note that when assemblies of different simulation rates become connected
via `Class.Constraint|Constraints` or collisions, the combined mechanism
will default to the highest simulation rate for stability.
property/Workspace/PhysicsSteppingMethod.title: PhysicsSteppingMethod

property/Workspace/PlayerCharacterDestro.description:
Controls whether the engine automatically calls `Destroy()` on a player's
character when it is replaced and on the `Player` object when the player
leaves.

When enabled, the engine automatically calls `Destroy()` on a player's old
character when it is replaced (for example, on respawn) and on the
`Class.Player` object itself when the player leaves the server.
property/Workspace/PlayerCharacterDestro.title: PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior

property/Workspace/PlayerScriptsUseInput.description:
Controls whether the built-in player scripts are updated to use the Input
Action System.

Controls whether the built-in player scripts are updated to use the
[Input Action System](../../../input/input-action-system.md). When
enabled, the player scripts live under `Class.StarterPlayer` (controlled
by `Class.StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule`) and the server is able
to process player inputs.
property/Workspace/PlayerScriptsUseInput.title: PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem

property/Workspace/PrimalPhysicsSolver.description:
Controls whether the experimental Primal Physics Solver is enabled.

The Primal Physics Solver is an experimental constraint solver that can
improve accuracy in complex setup. Setting this property to
`Enum.PrimalPhysicsSolver|Experimental` enables it.
property/Workspace/PrimalPhysicsSolver.title: PrimalPhysicsSolver

property/Workspace/RejectCharacterDeleti.description:
Controls whether the server rejects attempts by clients to delete player
characters from the workspace.

When enabled, the server ignores client requests to delete player
`Class.Model|character` objects from the workspace, preventing exploits
that attempt to abuse this replication path.
`Enum.RejectCharacterDeletions|Default` is currently equivalent to
`Enabled`.
property/Workspace/RejectCharacterDeleti.title: RejectCharacterDeletions

property/Workspace/RenderingCacheOptimiz.description:
Controls whether rendering cache optimizations are enabled.

Controls whether the engine caches rendering state data to reduce
redundant per-frame work. When enabled, the renderer can skip recomputing
state for static objects, improving frame rates in scenes with many parts.
property/Workspace/RenderingCacheOptimiz.title: RenderingCacheOptimizations

property/Workspace/ReplicateInstanceDest.description:
Controls how `Instance:Destroy()` calls are replicated from the server to
clients.

Determines the replication behavior when `Instance:Destroy()` is called on
the server. When `Enum.ReplicateInstanceDestroySetting|Enabled`, the
engine uses improved replication semantics for instance destruction.
property/Workspace/ReplicateInstanceDest.title: ReplicateInstanceDestroySetting

property/Workspace/Retargeting.description:
Controls whether animation retargeting is enabled for character
animations.

Sets the animation retargeting mode. Retargeting adapts animations to
character rigs of different proportions, allowing a single animation to
play correctly on characters of varying sizes and shapes.
property/Workspace/Retargeting.title: Retargeting

property/Workspace/SandboxedInstanceMode.description:
Controls whether sandboxed instance mode (script capabilities) is enabled.

When set to `Enum.SandboxedInstanceMode|Experimental`, the engine enables
sandboxed instance mode, which lets you use script capabilities.
property/Workspace/SandboxedInstanceMode.title: SandboxedInstanceMode

property/Workspace/SignalBehavior.description:
Configures when the engine resumes event handlers.

This property determines whether event handlers will be resumed
immediately when the event fires, or deferred and then resumed at a later
resumption point. Resumption points currently include:

- Input processing (resumes once per input to be processed, see
  `Class.UserInputService`)
- `Class.RunService.PreRender`
- Legacy waiting script resumption such as `wait()`, `spawn()`, and
  `delay()`
- `Class.RunService.PreAnimation`
- `Class.RunService.PreSimulation`
- `Class.RunService.PostSimulation`
- Waiting script resumption such as `Library.task.wait()`,
  `Library.task.spawn()`, and `Library.task.delay()`
- `Class.RunService.Heartbeat`
- `Class.DataModel.BindToClose`

For more information, see
[Deferred Events](../../../scripting/events/deferred.md).
property/Workspace/SignalBehavior.title: SignalBehavior

property/Workspace/StreamOutBehavior.description:
Configures how the engine decides when to stream content away from
players.

This property controls where content will be unloaded from the
`Class.Player.ReplicationFocus|ReplicationFocus` based on device memory
conditions, or based on the streaming radius.

#### See also

- `Class.Workspace.StreamingEnabled` which controls whether content
  streaming is enabled
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingMinRadius`
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingTargetRadius`
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingIntegrityMode`
property/Workspace/StreamOutBehavior.title: StreamOutBehavior

property/Workspace/StreamingEnabled.description:
Whether content streaming is enabled for the place.

This property determines whether in-experience content streaming is
enabled for the place. This property is not scriptable and therefore must
be set on the `Workspace` object in Studio.

#### See also

- `Class.Workspace.StreamingMinRadius`
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingTargetRadius`
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingIntegrityMode`
property/Workspace/StreamingEnabled.title: StreamingEnabled

property/Workspace/StreamingIntegrityMod.description:
Determines whether streaming integrity mode is active.

If instance [streaming](../../../workspace/streaming/index.md) is enabled,
an experience may behave in unintended ways if a player's character moves
into a region of the world that has not been streamed to their client. The
streaming integrity feature offers a way to avoid those potentially
problematic situations.
property/Workspace/StreamingIntegrityMod.title: StreamingIntegrityMode

property/Workspace/StreamingMinRadius.description:
Minimum distance that content will be streamed to players with high
priority.

This property indicates the radius around the player's character or the
current `Class.Player.ReplicationFocus|ReplicationFocus` in which content
will be streamed in at the highest priority. Defaults to 64 studs.

Care should be taken when increasing the default minimum radius since
doing so will require more memory and more server bandwidth at the expense
of other components.

#### See also

- `Class.Workspace.StreamingEnabled` which controls whether content
  streaming is enabled
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingTargetRadius`
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingIntegrityMode`
property/Workspace/StreamingMinRadius.title: StreamingMinRadius

property/Workspace/StreamingTargetRadius.description:
Maximum distance that content will be streamed to players.

This property controls the maximum distance away from the player's
character or the current `Class.Player.ReplicationFocus|ReplicationFocus`
in which content will be streamed in. Defaults to 1024 studs.

Note that the engine is allowed to retain previously loaded content beyond
the target radius, memory permitting.

#### See also

- `Class.Workspace.StreamingEnabled` which controls whether content
  streaming is enabled
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingMinRadius`
- `Class.Workspace.StreamingIntegrityMode`
property/Workspace/StreamingTargetRadius.title: StreamingTargetRadius

property/Workspace/Terrain.description: A reference to the `Class.Terrain` object parented to the `Class.Workspace`. This property is a reference to the `Class.Terrain` object parented to the `Class.Workspace`. See [Environmental Terrain](../../../parts/terrain.md) for more information.
property/Workspace/Terrain.title: Terrain

property/Workspace/TouchesUseCollisionGr.description:
Determines whether `Class.BasePart|parts` in different groups set to not
collide will ignore collisions and touch events.

This property determines whether `Class.BasePart|parts` in different
groups set to not collide will ignore collisions and touch events. By
default, the value of this property is set to `false`.

When this property is enabled, parts in different groups set to not
collide will also ignore the `Class.BasePart.CanTouch|CanTouch` property,
similar to how `Class.BasePart.CanCollide` is ignored. For more
information on the behavior of CanTouch, please visit its property page.
property/Workspace/TouchesUseCollisionGr.title: TouchesUseCollisionGroups

property/Workspace/UseFixedSimulation.description:
When `true`, enables `Class.RunService:BindToSimulation()` which calls a
function at a fixed frequency, updates physics stepping logic, and makes
the `Global.RobloxGlobals.time()` function return the fixed stepped frame
time.

When `true`, enables `Class.RunService:BindToSimulation()` which calls a
function at a fixed frequency. Also updates physics stepping logic such
that character controller updates and joint transforms are performed at a
fixed frequency rather than once per frame, as well as makes the
`Global.RobloxGlobals.time()` function return the fixed stepped frame
time.
property/Workspace/UseFixedSimulation.title: UseFixedSimulation

property/Workspace/UseNewLuauTypeSolver.description:
Controls whether the new Luau type solver is used for type inference.

This `Enum.RolloutState` property controls whether the new Luau type
solver is used for type inference and type checking in scripts. The new
type solver provides improved accuracy and performance for type analysis.
Note that `Class.Workspace.LuauTypeCheckMode` controls the mode (strict,
nonstrict, etc.) while this property controls which solver implementation
is active. `Enum.RolloutState|Default` follows the current engine-wide
rollout state.
property/Workspace/UseNewLuauTypeSolver.title: UseNewLuauTypeSolver

property/WrapLayer/AutoSkin.description:
Determines whether this WrapLayer automatically transfers skinning data
from the underlying body mesh to the clothing mesh.

Determines whether this WrapLayer automatically transfers skinning data
from the underlying body mesh to the clothing mesh. When set to
`Enum.WrapLayerAutoSkin.EnabledOverride|EnabledOverride`, skinning is
applied regardless of whether the clothing mesh already has skinning data.
When set to `Enum.WrapLayerAutoSkin.EnabledPreserve|EnabledPreserve`,
skinning is only applied if the mesh does not already have skinning data.

This property requires `Class.StarterPlayer.LoadCharacterLayeredClothing`
to be set to `Enabled` (or `Default`) in order to function. When layered
clothing is disabled, the auto-skinning pipeline does not run and this
property has no effect.

For more information, see
[Automatic Skinning Transfer](../../../avatar/automatic-skinning-transfer.md).
property/WrapLayer/AutoSkin.title: AutoSkin

property/WrapLayer/BindOffset.description:
`Datatype.CFrame` is used to adjust a binding point for clothing item
mesh. Could be used to move and rotate clothing items. This property is
intended for fine-tuning only and it is heavily optional.

This property is intended for fine-tuning purposes and is highly optional.

`Datatype.CFrame` to adjust a binding point for a clothing item mesh.
Allows for fine-tuning of clothing items (slight adjustment of
position/rotation to get a unique look) in contexts such as community-made
avatar editors.
property/WrapLayer/BindOffset.title: BindOffset

property/WrapLayer/Color.description:
Sets color used for the debug rendering. See `Class.WrapTarget.DebugMode`.

Sets color used for the debug rendering. See `Class.WrapTarget.DebugMode`
property/WrapLayer/Color.title: Color

property/WrapLayer/DebugMode.description:
Allows switching between different debugging visualization modes for cage
meshes.
property/WrapLayer/DebugMode.title: DebugMode

property/WrapLayer/Enabled.description:
Allows for disabling of the `Class.WrapLayer` object as if it does not
exist.
property/WrapLayer/Enabled.title: Enabled

property/WrapLayer/Order.description:
Controls the composition order for layered clothing.

Controls the composition order for layered clothing. Clothing items with
higher order will appear on top of clothing items with lower order. If two
items have the same order, the deformer composition order is ambiguous and
depends on serialization order. Default value is 1.
property/WrapLayer/Order.title: Order

property/WrapLayer/Puffiness.description:
Controls how much underlying clothing items inflate the current clothing
item.

Controls how much underlying clothing items inflate the current clothing
item.

Valid range is -1 to 1. A value of -1 compresses the clothing, body, and
all underlying layers such that the clothing itself takes the shape of the
body. A value of 0 makes the clothing item fit as if it was the only piece
of clothing being worn, compressing all underlying layers. A value of 1
(default) never compresses anything and infinitely inflates over
underlying clothing items.
property/WrapLayer/Puffiness.title: Puffiness

property/WrapLayer/ReferenceMeshContent.description:
The reference mesh that defines the Inner Cage of the `Class.WrapLayer`,
stored as a `Datatype.Content` value.

The reference mesh that defines the inner cage of a `Class.WrapLayer`,
stored as a `Datatype.Content` value. Together with the outer cage from
`Class.BaseWrap.CageMeshContent|CageMeshContent`, the inner cage describes
the surfaces used to fit and deform the accessory around an avatar and
underlying accessories without clipping. A `Class.WrapLayer` is only
considered valid once both its cage mesh and its reference mesh are set.

The reference mesh establishes the standard topology and UV coordinates
used for index matching. It is expected that for all catalog avatars this
points to one of the 15 standard reference meshes provided by Roblox, but
for some NPCs or a custom avatar system it might point to a different
mesh. This property is normally set up automatically by the Importer.

This `Datatype.Content`-typed property is the successor to
`Class.WrapLayer.ReferenceMeshId` and reads and writes the same underlying
storage. Defaults to an empty `Datatype.Content`.
property/WrapLayer/ReferenceMeshContent.title: ReferenceMeshContent

property/WrapLayer/ReferenceMeshId.description:
AssetID for reference mesh used to define Inner Cage of a 3D object.

AssetID for reference mesh used to define Inner Cage of a 3D object

Reference mesh is used to define standard topology and UV coordinates for
index matching. It is expected that for all catalog avatars, this will
point to one of 15 standard reference meshes provided by Roblox. But for
some NPCs or a custom avatar system, this might point to other meshes.

Note: this property is set up automatically by the FBX importer
property/WrapLayer/ReferenceMeshId.title: ReferenceMeshId

property/WrapLayer/ReferenceOrigin.description:
Reference mesh offset relative to parent MeshPart (in the parent MeshPart
space)

Note: this property is set up automatically by the FBX importer.

Reference mesh offset relative to parent MeshPart (in the parent MeshPart
space)

Note: this property is set up automatically by the FBX importer
property/WrapLayer/ReferenceOrigin.title: ReferenceOrigin

property/WrapLayer/ReferenceOriginWorld.description:
Reference mesh offset relative to parent MeshPart (in the world space)

Note: this property is set up automatically by the FBX importer.

Reference mesh offset relative to parent MeshPart (in the world space)

Note: this property is set up automatically by the FBX importer
property/WrapLayer/ReferenceOriginWorld.title: ReferenceOriginWorld

property/WrapLayer/ShrinkFactor.description:
Allows slight shrinking/expanding of the resulting render mesh, without
affecting any other layers.

This property is intended for fine-tuning purposes and is highly optional.

Allows slight shrinking/expanding of the resulting render mesh, without
affecting any other layers. This is useful in rare cases when the clothing
mesh does not precisely fit the underlying clothing layers (the cage is
usually slightly overestimated atop the real shape to avoid layer
interpenetration). Even slight overestimation has the tendency to
accumulate, especially when there are a lot of layers. While this is
usually not critical, some items like backpacks may be problematic.

Valid range is -1 to 1. A value of -1 will maximally expand while a value
of 1 will maximally shrink. A value of 0 (default) has no effect.
property/WrapLayer/ShrinkFactor.title: ShrinkFactor

property/WrapTarget/Color.description:
Sets color used for the debug rendering. See `Class.WrapTarget.DebugMode`.

Sets color used for the debug rendering. See `Class.WrapTarget.DebugMode`
property/WrapTarget/Color.title: Color

property/WrapTarget/DebugMode.description:
Allows switching between different debugging visualization modes for cage
meshes.
property/WrapTarget/DebugMode.title: DebugMode

property/WrapTarget/Stiffness.description:
Defines how much the body mesh can be compressed by clothing.

Defines how much the body mesh can be compressed by clothing. Super tight
clothing may lead to an intersection between the clothing mesh and body
mesh. To solve this visual artifact, the deformer can compress the body
mesh slightly to solve possible intersections.

Valid range is 0 to 1. A value of 0 will compress the body mesh as much as
necessary to ensure that the intersections are eliminated (visible body
parts might look a little bit deformed). A value of 1 will prevent the
body mesh from being compressed (may lead to visible intersections or
Z-fighting). A value of 0.9 (default) is a reasonable default that solves
most of the intersections without introducing any significant body
deformation.
property/WrapTarget/Stiffness.title: Stiffness

property/WrapTextureTransfer/ReferenceCa.description:
An optional reference mesh used for pruning and validating the target
cage.

The reference cage mesh is the cage mesh that the texture was authored
for. This target cage mesh defined in `Class.WrapTarget` is pruned against
this `ReferenceCageMeshContent`. If the target cage mesh contains vertices
or faces that are not present in the reference cage mesh, these vertices
and faces are removed from the target cage mesh before performing the
texture transfer. If there are no shared UVs between
`ReferenceCageMeshContent` and cage mesh defined in `Class.WrapTarget`,
the texture transfer fails.

When not defined, the cage in `Class.WrapTarget` in ancestor
`Class.MeshPart` is used for transfer without any pruning or validation.
property/WrapTextureTransfer/ReferenceCa.title: ReferenceCageMeshContent

property/WrapTextureTransfer/UVMaxBound.description:
Determines the maximum bound of the UV space to include in the transfer.

Determines the maximum bound of the UV space to include in the transfer.
Areas of the cage mesh with UV values greater than the maximum bound
aren't included when applying the texture.

The Decal textures apply to the parent `Class.MeshPart` with the textures
scaling linearly between UVMinBound and UVMaxBound.

When set to default -inf, the maximum UV value is used from WrapTarget's
cage.
property/WrapTextureTransfer/UVMaxBound.title: UVMaxBound

property/WrapTextureTransfer/UVMinBound.description:
Determines the minimum bound of the UV space to include in the transfer.

Determines the minimum bound of the UV space to include in the transfer.
Areas of the cage mesh with UV values smaller than the minimum bound
aren't included when applying the texture.

The Decal textures apply to the parent `Class.MeshPart` with the textures
scaling linearly between UVMinBound and UVMaxBound.

When set to default inf, uses the minimum UV value from WrapTarget's cage.
property/WrapTextureTransfer/UVMinBound.title: UVMinBound

rojo/Middleware.description:
Represents a possible 'transformer' used by Rojo to turn a file system
item into a Roblox Instance. Missing from this list is metadata.
This is deliberate, as metadata is not a snapshot middleware.
Directories cannot be used for sync rules so they're ignored by Serde.

rojo/PathNode.description: Describes a path that is either optional or required

rojo/Project.description:
Contains all of the configuration for a Rojo-managed project.
Project files are stored in `.project.json` files.

blockedPlaceIds.description:
If specified, contains a set of place IDs that this project is
not compatible with when doing live sync.
This setting is intended to help prevent syncing a Rojo project into the
wrong Roblox place.

emitLegacyScripts.description:
Determines if Rojo should emit scripts with the appropriate `RunContext`
for `*.client.lua` and `*.server.lua` files in the project instead of
using `Script` and `LocalScript` Instances.

gameId.description:
If specified, sets the current place's game ID when connecting to the
Rojo server from Roblox Studio.

globIgnorePaths.description:
A list of globs, relative to the folder the project file is in, that
match files that should be excluded if Rojo encounters them.

name.description: The name of the top-level instance described by the project.

placeId.description:
If specified, sets the current place's place ID when connecting to the
Rojo server from Roblox Studio.

serveAddress.description:
If specified, this address will be used in place of the default address
As long as --address is unprovided.

serveAllowedHosts.description:
Additional `Host`/`Origin` header values that `rojo serve` will accept
beyond `localhost` and the bind address, such as a hostname like
`mypc.lan` used to reach a network-exposed server by name. Listing any
host also turns on `Host`/`Origin` validation for binds where it is
otherwise off (such as `0.0.0.0`). The `--allowed-hosts` CLI option
overrides this field when provided.

servePlaceIds.description:
If specified, contains the set of place IDs that this project is
compatible with when doing live sync.
This setting is intended to help prevent syncing a Rojo project into the
wrong Roblox place.

servePort.description:
If specified, sets the default port that `rojo serve` should use when
using this project for live sync.

syncRules.description:
A list of mappings of globs to syncing rules. If a file matches a glob,
it will be 'transformed' into an Instance following the rule provided.
Globs are relative to the folder the project file is in.

syncbackRules.description: A list of rules for syncback with this project file.

tree.description:
The tree of instances described by this project. Projects always
describe at least one instance.

rojo/ProjectNode.description: Describes an instance and its descendants in a project.

$className.description:
If set, defines the ClassName of the described instance.
`$className` MUST be set if `$path` is not set.
`$className` CANNOT be set if `$path` is set and the instance described
by that path has a ClassName other than Folder.

$id.description:
If set, defines an ID for the described Instance that can be used
to refer to it for the purpose of referent properties.

$ignoreUnknownInstances.description:
Defines the behavior when Rojo encounters unknown instances in Roblox
Studio during live sync. `$ignoreUnknownInstances` should be considered
a large hammer and used with care.
If set to `true`, those instances will be left alone. This may cause
issues when files that turn into instances are removed while Rojo is not
running.
If set to `false`, Rojo will destroy any instances it does not
recognize.
If unset, its default value depends on other settings:
- If `$path` is not set, defaults to `true`
- If `$path` is set, defaults to `false`

$path.description:
Defines that this instance should come from the given file path. This
path can point to any file type supported by Rojo, including Lua files
(`.lua`), Roblox models (`.rbxm`, `.rbxmx`), and localization table
spreadsheets (`.csv`).

$properties.description: The properties that will be assigned to the resulting instance.

rojo/SyncRule.description:
Represents an user-specified rule for transforming files
into Instances using a given middleware.

exclude.description: A pattern used to determine if a file is excluded from this SyncRule.

pattern.description: A pattern used to determine if a file is included in this SyncRule

suffix.description:
A suffix to trim off of file names, including the file extension.
If not specified, the file extension is the only thing cut off.

use.description: The middleware specified by the user for this SyncRule

createIgnoreDirPaths.description:
Whether the globs specified in `ignore_paths` should be modified to also
match directories. Defaults to `true`.
If this is `true`, it'll take ignore globs that end in `/**` and convert
them to also handle the directory they're referring to. This is
generally a better UX.

ignorePaths.description:
A list of patterns to check against the path an Instance would serialize
to. If a path matches one of these, the Instance won't be syncbacked.

ignoreProperties.description:
A map of classes to properties to ignore for that class when doing
syncback.

ignoreReferents.description:
Whether to skip serializing referent properties like `Model.PrimaryPart`
during syncback. Defaults to `false`.

ignoreTrees.description: A list of subtrees in a file that will be ignored by Syncback.

syncCurrentCamera.description:
Whether or not the `CurrentCamera` of `Workspace` is included in the
syncback or not. Defaults to `false`.

syncUnscriptable.description:
Whether or not to sync properties that cannot be modified via scripts.
Defaults to `true`.

rojo/UnresolvedValue.description:
A user-friendly version of `Variant` that supports specifying ambiguous
values. Ambiguous values need a reflection database to be resolved to a
usable value.
This type is used in Rojo projects and JSON models to make specifying the
most common types of properties, like strings or vectors, much easier.
